3.4 LACK OF REGULAR BUILDINGS FOR POLICE STATIONS
Recommendation
3.4.1 The Committee takes serious view of the fact that 72 police stations out of 180 police
stations are functioning without regular buildings. It is very unfortunate that in the Capital city
of the country, the Police stations are functioning without regular buildings. The Committee
recommends that the Government should take immediate steps to provide regular buildings to these
72 police stations at the earliest. (Para 4.2.20 ibid)
Action Taken
3.4.2 Presently, 108 Police Stations are running in regular buildings. 08 Police Stations are under
construction. The land in respect of 30 Police Stations is available. Remaining 34 Police Stations
have no land. Out of 30 police stations where land is available, the construction of 09 is at tender
stage, 01 is at final stage of tendering, 14 police stations are at planning stage and in 06 cases
land has been allotted, but possession has not been given so far. Further efforts are being made
by holding meetings regularly with the land owning agencies like MCD, DDA, NDMC, etc. for
allotment of land for Police Stations.
Further Recommendation
3.4.3 The Committee is not convinced with the reply and is of the considered view that the
functioning of Police Stations must be suffering due to the handicap that police stations are
not functioning from regular building. Indeterminate weather, safety of arms and
ammunition and security and preservation of records due to absence of permanent office
building for the police stations are the areas of major concern which can not be taken so
lightly. The Committee, therefore, recommends that construction of eight police stations be
completed without further delay and planning for the construction of regular building at 30
police stations, where land is available, be chalked out on priority and further possibility for
acquiring land for 30 police stations from MCD, DDA and NDMC, as the case may be, be
explored at the earliest for regular building for the police station at the respective places.
The Committee may be apprised of the development in this direction.
3.5 CRIME AGAINST WOMEN
Recommendation
3.5.1 As regards crime figures, the Committee takes serious note of the increasing cases of
molestation, rape and kidnapping during the last three years. The Committee is of the view that
prevention of crime against women should be a priority issue of the Delhi Police. The Committee
understands that most of the crimes against women go unreported due to non-cooperating attitude

48
of police personnel in Delhi. In view of this, the Committee recommends that more and more
women officers should be employed at lower as well as higher level in Delhi Police so that female
victims would approach them without hesitation. (Para 4.2.21 ibid)
Action Taken
3.5.2 Delhi Police has taken various steps for safety and security of women. These measures
include identifying the vulnerable areas requiring presence of adequate police staff, including
women police. To cover such areas prone to crime against women, lady police staff has been
deployed in beats and in PCR Vans. Two police stations predominantly staffed by women have been
opened in the North and South Campus. Women Help Desk have been formed in all police stations
and special measures have been taken for safety and security of women employees by issuing
directions under Section 144 Cr.P.C. to BPOs, Corporate and media houses for taking safety steps.
Gender sensitization programmes have been organized for police personnel. PCR Vans have been
directed to help stranded women. Delhi Police is also maintaining several helplines viz. the Women’s
helpline 1091 and the Anti-Obscene Call/Anti-stalking helpline 1096, which have received a good
response. Delhi police has also established Anti-Human Trafficking Units (AHTUs) in all Districts.
3.5.3 In order to enhance confidence of the public, including women all over the city, special
measures are introduced. These include creating of predominantly women staffed police stations at

appointed for handling problems of North Eastern women. Areas where there is a predominance
of North-East residents are identified and area police have orders to ensure that there is no illegal
activity/ harassment in these areas.
3.5.4 Delhi Police is committed to make the city a safe place for women. For this, we are taking
the following measures to prevent crime against women:–
(i) Orders for BPOs etc. for safety of women :- The Delhi Police has issued orders
U/s 144 Cr.P.C. directing the BPOs, Corporate and Media Houses for taking certain
steps for the safety and security of Women employees, like ensuring that they do not
travel alone in the cab and are dropped right at their door steps and accompanied by
the security guard.
(ii) Police presence at Bus stops :-  Over 300 Bus-stops saw police presence. Composite
teams from Police Stations, Traffic Units and the PCR teamed up to man police
pickets in identified areas.
(iii) Creation of Women Help-Desk :- Prominent help-desks are created to attend
women complainants in each Police Station.
(iv) Directions to PCR Van to help stranded women :- All PCR Vans are directed to
help stranded women during night. Any women can call PCR van by dialing 100 who
will be dropped to the nearest safe place.
(v) Women staff are deployed in beats and in PCR vans in the areas prone to crime
against women.
(vi) Surprise checks in buses, markets, cinema, road junctions, universities/colleges/
schools etc.
(vii) Gender Sensitization of Police personnel :- The Gender sensitization and legal
awareness programmes were organized for police personnel, in association with
reputed NGOs to create a ‘Gender-friendly Environment’ in police stations. SPUW&C

49
Nanak Pura has organized several programmes at PS and Subdivision level at various
Districts of Delhi with the help of NGO’s and large number of officers were trained.
(viii) Self-Defence Training :- 63 programmes were launched in various schools/colleges
and other institutions and 6730 girls/women were imparted self-defence training in the
year 2011. Since its inception in year 2002, as many as 605 programmes were
conducted in which more than 79549 girls/women were trained.
(ix) Liaison with Rape Crisis Intervention Centres :- A mechanism has been evolved
to maintain a close liaison between the local police and the District RCICs and their
members like Doctors, Psychologists, Lawyers, V olunteers Organizations, Nodal
Officers etc. by convening periodical meetings so as to facilitate providing
professional counseling to rape victims.
(x) Parivartan :- In this unique experiment women police officials are deputed to
perform beat duties and they are imparted special training to control crime against
women. Further this scheme includes educating parents, teachers, students, youths,
Area Security Committee members, NGOs and other key persons on issues pertaining
to safety of woman. The scheme also includes door-step policing by women
constables for identification and redressal of grievances of women within the
community; intensive street performances focusing on rape and sexual assault, dowry
harassment and domestic violence against women and awareness lectures by
psychologists to sensitize adolescent boys and girls about crime.
(xi) Establishment of women police station :-  Woman dominated police stations were

Nagar and South Campus respectively for the safety of girl students and for building
the confidence among them.
(xii) Speedy Trial of gang rape cases :-  On the request of Delhi Police, Hon’ble High

cases be fast tracked.

3.6 UNDER REPORTING OF RAPE AND MOLESTATION CASES
Recommendation
3.6.1 The Committee takes note of the fact that the figures given by Delhi Police do not match
the cases reported in media about rape and molestation. Stringent action should be taken against
the culprits involved in harassing girls. The Committee understands that merely counting the
number of incidents does not justify the general perception. The Committee believes that a mass
campaign should be organised by Delhi Police against such incidents. (Para 4.2.22 ibid)
Action Taken
3.6.2 Maximum attention is paid to solving the incidents of rape and other crimes against women
in Delhi. All out efforts are made to bring the perpetrators of such crimes to book. During the year
2011, the work-out percentage of rape cases in Delhi was as high as 97.5% and of molestation
cases 95.4%. Investigation in these cases is carried out in most professional manner so that the
accused persons are properly linked to the Crime. Delhi Police also follow-up on the bail matters
of such accused in the Courts, so that the criminals do not get bailed out easily. On the request
of Delhi Police, Hon’ble High Court Delhi has issued directions to the District Courts in Delhi that
all gang rape cases be fast tracked.
3.6.3 In addition to the above, Women Sub-Inspectors have been designated to investigate cases
of rape exclusively so that victims can approach and confide in them un-hesitatingly. Special
courses are being conducted for these officers in investigation of women related cases.
3.6.4 Reporting of kidnapping cases had increased due to direction of Hon’ble High Court Delhi,
for registering FIR in every missing girl of age upto 18 years and for boy upto 16 years. In
kidnapping cases the detection rate was 54.4% in 2009 which improved to 70.7% in year 2011.
The strength of women police staff has been increased in police stations.
Further Recommendation
3.6.5 Delhi Police is required to be more alert all the time and should give impetus on the
preventive measures for non-occurance of such incidents. The incidents of kidnapping also
needs to be curbed and such cases are to be handled more proficiently.

Recommendation

force. The Committee feels that merely advising the States/UTs to have their own Specialist
Response Force for responding to disasters will not serve the purpose. The Committee impresses

rd and 4 th

rd and 4 th Line Maintenance of BSF helicopters at 3 Base Repair

Recommendation
4.8.1 The Committee notes with displeasure that NIDM is still functioning from a rented premises
of Indian Institute of Public Administration. The Committee is unable to understand the inordinate
delay in the matter of providing land to the Institute. Now that the land has been identified by
Delhi Development Authority, the Government should take possession of the land at the earliest
and start construction of the building without further delay. The Committee further recommends
that all the 124 posts in NDMA be filled up at the earliest. The Committee also recommends that

64
review of the Disaster Management Act may be completed at the earliest so as to have a more
efficient and implementable legislation in the country. (Para 5.1.15 ibid)

demand letter for provisional premium amount of Rs.5,40,97,551.00 for the land at Rohini.  Amount
has been sanctioned. It is expected that NIDM will get the possession of this land very soon.

posts in NDMA.

Disaster Management Act, 2005 under the chairmanship of Dr. P.K. Mishra, former Secretary,
Department of Agriculture & Cooperation, Ministry of Agriculture, Government of India and
presently Chairman, Gujarat Electricity Regulatory Commission, Gujarat. The Terms of Reference
(TOR) of the Task Force is as under:
(i) To gather information from States/UTs/other Stakeholders regarding concerns/
limitations being faced by the States/UTs in implementation/administration of the
Disaster Management Act, 2005.
(ii) To study the existing such Acts/best practices on the subject globally and consider its
adoption in Indian scenario.
(iii) To consult and hold workshops on Regional/National levels to discuss with States/
UTs/Stakeholders regarding the implementation/administration of the Act in the States/
UTs and the imperative need, if any, towards amendments in the Disaster Management
Act, 2005.
(iv) To suggest necessary modifications/ amendments, if any, in the Disaster Management
Act, 2005 based on suggestions and deliberations with States/UTs/other Stakeholders.
(v) The Task Force has already held 3 meetings and finalised & circulated Questionnaire
on DM Act, 2005 for inviting comments of States/UTs, Central Ministries/Departments
and other stakeholders. The Questionnaire has been posted on MHA’s website also for

4.9 REVISION OF PRIME MINISTER’S PACKAGE FOR KASHMIRI MIGRANTS
Recommendation
4.9.1 The Committee notes that revision of the PM Package is underway. The Committee
recommends that the Prime Minister package should be revisited as a whole, to make it more
implementable and attractive. (Para 5.2.8 ibid)

65
4.9.2 The Committee is pleased to know that the Ministry has accorded approval of the PM’ s
package amounting to Rs.1618.40 crore for Relief and Rehabilitation of Kashmiri Migrants which
would help rehabilitation measures such as housing, transit accommodation, continuation of cash
relief, employment, assistance to agriculturists/horticulturists and waiver of interest loans aiming
for homecoming of J and K Migrants. The Committee is happy to know that the State Government
has invited applications from migrants interested in returning to the Valley. (Para 5.2.9 ibid)
4.9.3 However, the Committee recommends that the Home Ministry should impress upon the State
Government for expediting construction of remaining units of transit accommodation meant for
J&K migrants. The Committee also recommends that 3000 posts exclusively meant for Kashmiri
migrants should be filled at the earliest. The Committee observes that the efforts of State as well
as Central Government for the return of Kashmiri Pandit migrants to Kashmir are proving futile
as only one migrant family has returned to the Valley even after two years of sanctioning of Prime
Minister’ s package for their return and rehabilitation. The Committee is of the view that it is the
responsibility of the Centre as well as state government for creating an atmosphere where these
migrants could feel safe after their return to the valley. (Para 5.2.10 ibid)
Action Taken
4.9.4 The Prime Minister’s Package for return and rehabilitation of Kashmiri migrants was
announced in April, 2008. The State Government has constituted as Apex Advisory Committee in
September, 2009 under the Chairmanship of the Revenue Minister to oversee the effective
implementation of the Package. The State Government has been able to partially implement only
two components of the package i.e. construction of transit accommodation and employment
component exclusively for the migrants. The State Government has taken up construction of 505
transit accommodation out of which 389 units have been completed. The remaining units are
expected to be completed by end of August, 2012. The State Government has also created 3000
posts exclusively for the Kashmiri migrants and so far, appointment orders have been issued in
respect of 2184 candidates out of which 1446 have joined in the Valley. The State Government has
submitted the revised package duly approved by State Cabinet to MHA for approval. The same is
being examined. The State Government has informed that the groups representing the Kashmiri
migrants have reservations in returning to Valley and settle at their native place.
4.9.5 The Apex Advisory Committee constituted for implementation of the package in their
meeting held on 03.09.2011 moved a resolution appreciating the Government for construction of
township of Jagati, implementation of employment components and construction of transit
accommodation. The members were informed that the community has to take a decision and reach
consensus about their return to Valley. The members were also informed that the Government has
already taken confidence building measures like implementation of employment component and
construction of transit accommodation etc. and the process shall continue. The Revenue Minister
also informed the Committee that whatever facilities are required for permanent settlement of
migrants in the Valley shall be made available to them.
4.9.6 The issues regarding effective implementation of the PM’s package was also reviewed in
a meeting chaired by Home Secretary on 19.09.2011 with the State Government.
4.9.7 The observation of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on the
161
st Report was also conveyed to the State Government.
Further Recommendation
4.9.8 The Committee is of the considered view that effective confidence building measures
by the Government would remove the reservations of the Kashmiri Migrants in returning

66
to valley and settle at their respective places. The Committee, therefore, reiterates its
recommendation that the Ministry of Home Affairs should impress upon the State
Government for timely implementation of Prime Minister’s package consisting of
implementation of employment program, construction of transit accommodation and other
facilities required for permanent settlement of J&K migrants in the  valley.

4.13 INDUSTRIAL POLLUTION IN V API
Recommendation
4.13.1 The issue of release of industrial effluents by chemical units in Vapi being released in the
Ganga river of Daman should be resolved soon. (Para 5.4.23(i) ibid)
Action Taken
4.13.2 Daman Ganga River is mostly getting polluted due to discharge of effluents from Vapi area
through the common effluent treatment plant (CETP) located at Vapi. The Central Government had
declared Vapi as critically polluted Industrial zone and had imposed a moratorium on consideration
of projects to be located there for Environmental Clearance. However the Central Government later
lifted the moratorium after taking into consideration the action plan submitted by Gujarat Pollution
Control Board for the Vapi Industrial Estate.  The Pollution Control Committee, Daman has taken
up the matter with the Chairman, Central Pollution Control Board highlighting the issues of pollution
in river Daman Ganga and requested to provide a copy  of approved revised action plan  for Vapi
(Gujarat), submitted by Gujarat Pollution Control Board and also provide information on the
measures to reduce pollution level in river Daman Ganga as a result of release of effluents from
CETP, Vapi and also requested to constitute a committee consisting of the officials belonging to
Gujarat Pollution Board and Pollution  Control Committee, DD and DNH for regular monitoring of
said action plan. Response from CPCB in this regard is awaited.

steps to reduce the power tarrifs in Daman and Diu.

1
REPORT
The Action Taken Report of the Committee deals with the action taken by the Ministry of
Development of North Eastern Region on the recommendations contained in the One Hundred and
Sixty-second Report of the Committee on Demands for Grants (2012-13) of the Ministry.  The One
Hundred Sixty-second Report was presented to Rajya Sabha /laid on the Table of Lok Sabha, on
the 7
th May 2012.
2. Action Taken Notes as received from the Ministry of DoNER in respect of the
recommendations contained in the Report have been categorized as follows:
Chapter I:  The recommendations/observations, which have been accepted by the
Government: Para Nos. 2.1.3, 2.2.2, 3.2.8, 2.4.11, 2.4.12, 2.5.4, 2.6.14, 2.7.7, 2.8.10,
2.9.5, 2.9.6, 2.10.5, 2.11.5, 2.15.4, 2.16.5, 2.17.5, 2.17.6, 3.3.4, 3.3.5, 3.5.5, 3.6.2,  (of
One Hundred Sixty-second Report) Total recommendations-21
The Committee is pleased to note that the Ministry has accepted its twenty one
recommendations as mentioned in Chapter-I of the Report.
Chapter II:  The recommendations/observations which the Committee does not desire to
pursue in view of the Government’s replies: Para Nos. 2.1.6, 2.1.9, 2.12.8, 2.12.9, 2.14.3,
2.17.7, 2.17.10, 3.1.4 ( ibid) Total recommendations-8
The Committee is convinced with the explanations furnished by the Ministry and,
therefore, does not want to pursue the recommendations further.
Chapter III:  The recommendations/observations in respect of which the Committee is
not satisfied with the replies of the Ministry: Para Nos.  2.3.2, 2.7.8, 2.8.11, 2.9.7, 2.11.7,
2.13.6, 3.2.9, 3.2.15 ( ibid) Total recommendations-8
The Committee expresses its concern over the non-implementation of its
recommendations contained in Chapter-III and desires that the Ministry should furnish
convincing action taken steps  in respect of those recommendations.
Chapter IV : The recommendations/observations in respect of which final replies of the
Government have not been received: Para Nos. 3.4.11, 3.4.12, 3.4.13, 3.4.14, 3.4.15 ( ibid)
Total recommendations-5
3. In respect of seven recommendations in Chapter-IV , the Ministry has either furnished
interim reply or couched its response in vague terms. Therefore, the Committee desires that the
Ministry should furnish pointed and detailed Action Taken Notes in respect of the recommendation
categorized in Chapter-IV in keeping with the spirit of the recommendations.
4. The details of the ATNs have been analyzed in various Chapters in the succeeding chapters.

2
CHAPTER-I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS WHICH
HA VE BEEN ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT
1.1 NON-PLAN SCHEME
RECOMMENDATION
1.1.1 The Committee hopes that earmarked plan outlay would prove sufficient for the purpose
and wherever the plan outlay becomes insufficient at a later stage, requisite amount would be
enhanced at RE stage. The Committee also desires that economy measures would be adhered to as
per Government of India guidelines so far non-plan outlay is concerned. The Committee also notes
that plan allocation in BE 2011-12 was substantially reduced at RE 2011-12 stage. The Committee
takes a serious note of this. The Committee would, however, discuss under each scheme separately.
(Para 2.1.3 of 162
nd Report)
Action Taken
1.1.2 Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region scrupulously adheres to the economy
instructions which are issued from time to time for economising non-plan expenditure. It is
constant endeavour of the Ministry to make the budgetary process as realistic as possible.
1.2 COMPARATIVE STUDY OF TENTH AND ELEVENTH FIVE YEAR PLANS
RECOMMENDATION
1.2.1 The Committee observes that against the total plan allocation made to the tune of
Rs. 5800.00 crore in Tenth Five Year Plan, the actual expenditure was to the tune of Rs. 5767.58
crore; which can be termed satisfactory. However, during the Eleventh Five Year Plan against the
Plan proposals of Rs. 14409.08 crore, the actual allocation has been confined at the level of
Rs. 7705.22 crore. The drastic reductions in respect of NLCPR, NEC, Development of roads in NE
States do not present good picture on the approach of the Government so far as development of
NE States is concerned. This only indicates that either the Ministry of DoNER could not justify
its proposals or after making proposals it was not able to implement the proposals. In both cases,
the looser has been the laggard NE region. The Committee feels that reduction in the plan
allocation in NE region defeated set target of the Government to put the socio-econosmic
development of region on fast track. The Committee would, however, deal each scheme separately
later in the report. (Para 2.2.2 ibid)
Action Taken
1.2.2 Ministry of Civil Aviation have requested Airports Authority of India, who are handling the
development of existing airports in the North Eastern Region, to set up a special Cell to monitor
the development activities of the airports in NER.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION
1.2.3 The Committee desires to be informed of the present status of the cell.
2

3
1.3 NORTH-EASTERN COUNCIL
RECOMMENDATION
1.3.1 The Committee observes that allocated amount in BE 2012-13 under Major Heads 2552 and
3601 is intended to liquidate the liabilities created during 11 th Five Year Plan and to take up new
Schemes during 12 th Five Year Plan. The Committee hopes that the earmarked allocation would
meet gap areas from the regional economic development perceptive and would achieve desired
results and physical targets. The Committee also hopes that the Ministry of DoNER would act as
a facilitator and co-ordinator between the NE States and central Government and the resilient NEC
Monitoring mechanism would be quite helpful in achieving the financial and physical targets
without any procrastination. (Para 2.4.11 ibid)
Action Taken
1.3.2 As observed by the Standing Committee, Monitoring mechanism in place in North Eastern
Council would be instrumental in achieving the financial and physical targets without any
procrastination.
RECOMMENDATION
1.3.3 The Committee desires that no scheme should suffer for want of fund. The Committee also
recommends that the Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance to approve projected
demands of NEC during the 12
th Five Year Plans. (Para 2.4.12 ibid)
Action Taken
1.3.4 Planning Commission has finalized GBS allocation at current prices totalling Rs. 6,108
crores in respect of NEC for 12th Plan.
1.4 CONSTRUCTION/IMPROVEMENT OF ROADS OF ECONOMIC IMPORTANCE
RECOMMENDATION
1.4.1 The Committee understands that economic importance roads are sine-qua-non for overall
progress of the NE region. The Committee, however, wonders that work of construction of
Mahadev-Tolloi-Pfutsero road still remain incomplete for want of takers i.e. denial by State
Government of Manipur for completion of projects. The Committee does not understand why the
State Government of Manipur refused to implement the project. All the States should cooperate to
implement the projects for an even development in NE Region. Now that the Ministry of Defence
has asked BRO to complete the balance work, the Committee hopes that the remaining work of
the undertaken projects would be completed during current financial year for which Rs. 7.00 crore
has been earmarked. (Para 2.5.4 ibid)
Action Taken
1.4.2 The balance work has since been commenced by the BRO and is expected to be completed
in two years.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION
1.4.3 The Committee notes the reply and recommends that necessary steps be taken to
avoid cost and time over run of the construction of the road. Efforts should be made to
complete in two years.

4
1.5 NON PLAN LOANS TO NORTH EASTERN HANDICRAFTS AND HANDLOOMS
DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION (NEHHDC)
RECOMMENDATION
1.5.1 The Committee underlines the pioneer role of NEHHDC in promotion and development of
handicrafts and handloom in NER. Therefore, the first and the foremost priority of the Government
in this sector should be higher budgetary provision for implementing the revival plan of the
corporation. A token provision of Non-plan loan to the tune of Rs. 2.00 crore in RE 2011-12 as well
as in BE 2012-13 is certainly not going to serve the intended purpose. The Committee hails the
promotional role of NEHHDC in developing and proclaiming inputs for products and design
developments, upgradation of technology and providing marketing infrastructure of the finished
products which ultimately results in better benefits to weavers and artisans of the region. The
Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the Ministry of DoNER should leave no stone
unturned in persuading the Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance for allocating higher
budgetary provision for revival scheme of the Corporation. The Committee hopes that the Corporation
would get the green signal for revival plan which is presently under active consideration of the Board
of Reconstruction of Public Sector Enterprises (BRPSE). (Para 2.6.14 ibid)
Action Taken
1.5.2 BRPSE has since recommended a revival plan for NEHHDC. Necessary procedural
formalities are in progress to operationalise the revival plan.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION
1.5.3 The Committee notes the reply and recommends that the revival plan for NHHDC be
operationalised at the earliest.
1.6 LOAN TO NORTH EASTERN REGIONAL AGRICULTURAL MARKETING
CORPORATION (NERAMAC)
RECOMMENDATION
1.6.1 The Committee commends the pivotal role of NERAMAC in encouraging food processing
units in NER and providing basic infrastructure for marketing of agricultural and allied products.
The Committee also feels that involvement of NERAMAC in Post-Harvest Technology Mission,
National Horticulture Mission and Bamboo Mission makes it necessary to expand the horizon of
its activities. Although NERAMAC continues to be a profit-making organization with net profit of
Rs. 1.47 crore during 2010-11, but meagre provision of Rs. 2.00 crore in RE 2011-12 and
BE 2012-13 is not sufficient for growth plan of the organization. The Committee, therefore,
recommends that the Ministry of DoNER may pursue for higher budgetary allocation to the
organization for its exponential growth. (Para 2.7.7 ibid)
Action Taken
1.6.2 Ministry of Finance will be told about inadequacy of budget allocations at the time of RE
finalization stage.
1.6.3 The target of turnover as per Memorandum of Understanding vis-à-vis  working capital
received during the financial years 2007-08 to 2011-12 is given below:

5
Financial Year Target of Actual turnover Working
Turnover as Achieved Capital Loan
per MoU Received
(Good Column)
2007-08 14.35 29.55 3.13
2008-09 23.00 36.91 2.00
2009-10 27.00 89.90 2.00
2010-11 50.00 101.47 2.00
2011-12 95.00 100.18 2.00
1.6.4 An analysis of trends in net profit and accumulated losses/profit of NERAMAC reveals that
the accumulated losses will wipe out by 2015-16 and corporation will turn into a profit making
company. However, there is a need to increase working capital loan for faster growth of the
corporation and Ministry is working on it.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION
1.6.5 The Committee is happy to note that the accumulated losses of NERAMAC will be
wiped out by 2015-16. The Committee recommends that the working capital loan
requirements as sought be by the Ministry, may be considered positively by the Ministry of
Finance and Planning Commission.
1.7 NORTH EASTERN DEVELOPMENT FINANCE CORPORATION LIMITED (NEDFi)
RECOMMENDATION
1.7.1 The Committee observes that North Eastern Development Finance Corporation Limited
(NEDFi) plays a significant role as lending institution. Since the corporation has been receiving
ever increasing demand for financial assistance for new projects, it has ambitious growth plan to
expand its business to 30 per cent on year to year basis. The Committee notes that the corporation
is projecting internal resource generation of around Rs. 290.00 crore, marketing borrowing of
Rs. 125.00 crore and soft loan of Rs. 30.00 crore from Ministry of DoNER. The Committee also
notes that limited resources at its disposal is posing a big constraint to meet the commitment of
revised disbursement target to the tune of RS. 485.00 crore during the financial year 2012-13. The
Committee recommends that adequate fund may be provided to NEDFi at RE stage to carry out
its activities smoothly. (Para 2.8.10 ibid)
Action Taken
1.7.2 Planning Commission has provided Rs. 60.00 crore as interest-free loan to NEDFi  during
2012-13.
1.8 NON-LAPSABLE CENTRAL POOL OF RESOURCES (NLCPR)
RECOMMENDATION
1.8.1 The Committee understands the tremendous role of NLCPR Scheme in developing
infrastructure of NE region to ensure economic sustainability of the region. However, the Committee

6
is constrained to express its displeasure to observe that till 31 st March, 2012 a total of 1337.00
infrastructure projects worth Rs. 10863.29 crore were approved out of which only 645 projects worth
Rs. 3531.00 have been completed which is just 48.24 per cent. The Committee further observes that
several projects taken up since 1998-99 under NLCPR are lagging behind. For example three
projects out of seventy projects on roads and bridges in Arunachal Pradesh; eighty four projects
out of two hundred ten projects on roads and bridges in Assam; one project out of fourteen projects
on health and seventeen projects out of forty six projects on water supply in Manipur; and five
projects out of twenty three projects on education in Meghalaya have been completed. The
performance is not convincing at all. (Para 2.9.5 ibid)
Action Taken
1.8.2 To expedite accelerated completion of projects, Non-Lapsable Central Pool of Resources
(NLCPR) Committee has since reviewed the progress of projects in all 8 (eight) North Eastern
States with State Government Officers during its 105th, 106th, 107th and 108th meetings held
during 17.05.2012 to 27.08.2012. NLCPR Committee expressed its concern over slow
implementation of projects and advised the States to ensure timely completion of projects. States
have also been advised to give focused attention to delayed projects and timely transfer of funds
to the implementing agencies. State Governments were also advised to plan the projects schedule
in such a way so that maximum utilization of working season could be made.
1.8.2 Hon’ble Minister of State (IC), DoNER has also reviewed progress of projects during his
visits to North Eastern States and stressed the need for expediting the implementation, specially of
delayed projects for faster development of North Eastern Region.
1.8.3 Resultantly, number of completion of projects has increased to 683 nos. The NLCPR
Committee has decided to review the implementation of projects in all eight NE States every year
to ensure timely implementation of projects by states.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION
1.8.4 The Committee notes the steps taken by the Ministry to review the progress of
projects and expedite their completion under NLCPR and recommends that proactive
measures be continued to achieve satisfactory completion of all the projects.
RECOMMENDATION
1.8.5 The Committee is not in agreement with the argument put forth for the delay in completion
of projects under NLCPR viz delay in utilization and transfer of funds to implementing agencies
by the State Government, problem being faced in acquisition of land, law and order situation
including insurgency; delay in awarding the work/tender. The Committee is of the considered view
that the Ministry of DoNER, as co-ordinator and facilitator must resolve issues concerning timely
implementation of projects. For this, Ministry of DoNER should review the existing monitoring
mechanism, which appears to be only on papers to ensure it to be more result oriented. The
Ministry should also persuade all the State Governments in NE to co-operate in the implementation
of NLCPR Schemes in the interest of economic development of the region. (Para 2.9.6 ibid)
Action Taken
1.8.6 To further strengthen monitoring mechanism, apart from site visits by officers of Ministry
of DoNER and periodical reports, Ministry is in process of appointment of Independent Quality
Monitors (IQM) for inspection of the projects. The proper follow up on the reports of IQM shall
be ensured for proper and timely implementation of projects.

7
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION
1.8.7 The Committee while appreciating the move of the Ministry recommends that
Independent Quality Monitors of good repute be appointed at the earliest.
1.9 BODOLAND TERRITORIAL COUNCIL (BTC)
RECOMMENDATION
1.9.1 The Committee notes that out of sanctioned amount of Rs. 476.27 crore, an amount of
Rs. 450.77 crore has been released. However, utilization certificates for an amount of Rs. 409.88
crore only have been received. The Committee recommends that BTC/State Government may be
asked to submit utilization certificates in respect of the balance amount at the earliest and the issue
of completion of remaining 16 projects be followed up proactively. The Committee welcomes
additional BTC package of Rs. 250.00 crore and recommends that work on sanctioned 15 projects
be completed at the earliest. The Committee further recommends that the State Government of
Assam may be persuaded to expedite DPRs on the four remaining projects so that work on these
projects could be started soon. (Para 2.10.5 ibid)
Action Taken
1.9.2 BTC Package of Rs. 500.00 crore:
State Government has been requested for expediting submission of utilization certificates of
the funds released and timely completion of the project. As on date, State Government has
submitted utilization certificate for Rs.410.65 crore against Rs.450.77 crore released. State
Government has also submitted completion certificates for 27 projects totalling Rs.254.28
crore.
1.9.3 Additional BTC Package of Rs.250.00 crore:
Out of 19 projects retained at an estimated cost of Rs.243.20 crore under this additional
package, 17 projects at approved cost of Rs.209.18 crore have been sanctioned and an
amount of Rs. 97.48 crore have been released so far. DPRs along with recommendations
of State Level Standing Committee (SLSC) only for remaining 2 projects are awaited from
Government of Assam.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION
1.9.4 The Committee notes the reply and recommends that the utilization certificates in
respect of remaining amount of about Rs. 40 crores be obtained at the earliest. The
Committee also recommends that effective monitoring of implementation of projects under
additional BTC package be ensured and the State Government of Assam may be impressed
upon to submit the two remaining DPRs at the earliest.
1.10 ADVERTISING AND PUBLICITY
RECOMMENDATION
1.10.1 The Committee notes that the outcome budget 2012-13 of the Ministry also mentions that
physical outputs in respect of Advertising and Publicity are not measurable/quantifiable. The
Committee is not convinced with the submission of the Ministry. The Committee recommends that
suitable mechanism may be evolved to ensure that physical outputs could be measurable in every
Plan Scheme not specifically the scheme under reference. (Para 2.11.5 ibid)

8
Action Taken
1.10.2 The observation made by the Committee has been noted. Ministry’s Action Plan under the
Advertising and Publicity Scheme is being finalized soon. This will reflect physical targets like
(i) number of advertisements to be released in print/electronic/outdoor media etc. during the year
(2012-13), (ii) maximum number of business summits/workshops/expos/seminars to be sponsored
and (iii) copies of books to be printed for publicity etc. These would, however, be tentative only
as exact quantitative targets in respect of events mentioned above can not be fixed as sponsorship
depends on (a) receipt of suitable/fit proposals from agencies outside the Ministry and
(b) availability of funds during the financial year. Therefore, a maximum range of action would be
indicated based on previous experiences of the Ministry and allocation of funds for the purpose
under the scheme.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION
1.10.3 The Committee while noting the reply impress upon the Ministry that every effort
be made on continuous basis to achieve the target set in the Ministry’s Action Plan of the
years to come.
1.11 CONSULTANCY, MONITORING, THIRD PARTY EV ALUATION CHARGES ETC.
UNDER NLCPR SCHEME
RECOMMENDATION
1.11.1 The Committee is pleased to note that in pursuance of its recommendation in its 149 th
Report, the Government has come forward with provision in the Budget for taking up Third Party
monitoring of NLCPR projects during 2011-12. The Committee notes with concern that a total of
91 projects were sent to State Governments for taking up third party monitoring which are yet to
be completed. The Committee also recommends that all the projects should be assessed without
further delay and be subjected to monitoring. (Para 2.15.4 ibid)
Action Taken
1.11.2 The response of State Governments of North Eastern Region for Third Party Monitoring of
projects by Independent Review and Monitoring Agencies (IRMA) introduced under NLCPR
scheme, in line with JNNURM scheme of Ministry of Urban Development, was poor. Out of 8
States only 2 States i.e. Arunachal Pradesh and Mizoram have submitted their proposals, but since
the proposals were incomplete and without proper tendering procedures, they were rejected.
1.11.3 In view of poor response from State Governments, Ministry of DoNER have decided to
appoint third party monitors on its own called as Independent Quality Monitors (IQM). The process
of appointment of IQM has already been initiated. It is expected to further strengthen monitoring
of projects implementation.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION
1.11.4 The Committee while appreciating the move of the Ministry recommends that
Independent Quality Monitors of good repute be appointed at the earliest.
1.12 NON-LAPSABLE CENTRAL POOL OF RESOURCES (NLCPR)- CENTRAL
RECOMMENDATION
1.12.1 The Committee welcomes the introduction of NLCPR-Central Plan Scheme. The Committee

9
notes the justification of the scheme as in the present set up, funding is not sufficient to speed
up the infrastructure development in NER. The Committee hopes that all infrastructure projects
would be completed within stipulated time-frame to further speed up development of NE States.
(Para 2.16.5 ibid)
Action Taken
1.12.2 Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region will make all out efforts for timely
completion of projects under NLCPR-Central Scheme as it will be implemented by the Central
Ministries.
1.13 NORTH EASTERN STATES ROADS INVESTMENT PROGRAMME
RECOMMENDATION
1.13.1 The Committee notes that Asian Development Bank assisted NERSIP has now taken final
shape to be launched for the benefit of NE States. The Committee hopes that the projects under
the scheme will be implemented in the right earnest with effective monitoring. (Para 2.17.5 ibid)
Action Taken
1.13.2 The Ministry is closely monitoring the progress made by the States for implementation of
the scheme. On 9th July 2012, Government of India and Asian Development Bank have signed
agreement for the Tranche 1 loan amount of US $ 74.8 million. Under Tranche 1, a total of 201.8 km

RECOMMENDATION
1.16.1 North East has huge potential for development of hydro-electric power, given its unique
natural advantage. The Committee is disappointed to know that as on March, 2012, 93.06% of the
capacity of the region still remains untapped. Slow progress of civil works, heavy rain, frequent
bandhs etc. are cited as reasons for delay. The Committee, while taking into account the handicaps
faced by the agencies, still believes that they cannot explain gross under utilization of power
potential in the region even after six decades of independence of the country. The policy of
reducing the eligibility to avail mega project benefits from 1000 MW to 700 MW in certain special
category States of J&K, Sikkim and the seven states of North East is a step in right direction. The
Committee would like to recommend that revised National Water Policy be finalized at the earliest.

and interventions suggested by it may be examined threadbare and necessary steps may be taken

sericulture plantation, aquaculture, poultry, dairy etc. in the NE states by utilizing the funds
provided by Government of India as interest-free loan in the 12
th Five Year Plan.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION
3.3.3 The Committee is dismayed over the evasive and vague reply. For achieving physical
targets, meeting the financial targets is also required. This aspect may be kept in mind.
3.4 NON-LAPSABLE CENTRAL POOL OF RESOURCES (NLCPR)
RECOMMENDATION
3.4.1 The Committee is given to understand that there are about 729 on-going projects wherein
grant of about Rs. 2309.00 crore is to be released for which higher allocation will be required.
The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Planning Commission and the Ministry of Finance
should assess the requirement of fund under NLCPR and accordingly accord approval of required
fund. (Para 2.9.7 ibid)
Action Taken
3.4.2 Planning Commission has approved an enhanced allocation of Rs. 6,048.70 crore for the
scheme during 12
th Five Year Plan.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION
3.4.3 The Committee expresses its displeasure on the vague reply of the Ministry and feels
that such replies handicap the Committee to plead strongly the Ministry’s case for enhanced
allocation, as the higher allocation under NLCPR is the key to ensure economic
sustainability of the region.
3.5 ADVERTISING AND PUBLICITY
RECOMMENDATION
3.5.1 The Committee notes that the Ministry has recommended for extension of LTC facility in
lieu of Home Town beyond 1
st May, 2012. The Committee also notes with appreciation that the
facility has further been extended for years. The Committee, however, desires that relaxation in
the matter of performing air journey by any airlines other than Air India, as has been extended
in case of LTC visit to J&K, may also be extended to meet the demand of seats in flights.
(Para 2.11.7 ibid)
Action Taken
3.5.2 Ministry of Development of North Eastern Region (DoNER) took up the matter with
Department of Personnel and Training (DoP&T), of allowing Government employees to perform air
journey to visit NER on LTC by any airlines other than Air India as in case of visit to J&K on
LTC. Department of Personnel and Training, while conveying their ‘No Objection’ to the proposal
advised this Ministry to take concurrence of Ministry of Civil Aviation and Department of

23
Expenditure. Accordingly, Ministry of DoNER approached Ministry of Civil Aviation and Department
of Expenditure but they have not agreed to the proposal.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION
3.5.3 The Committee is of the view that permission to Government employees to visit
NER on LTC by any airlines other than Air India as in the case of visit to J&K would
attract larger number of Government employees which would generate revenue to NER.
Therefore, Ministry of DoNER should pursue the matter again with the Ministry of Civil
Aviation and Department of Expenditure. The admissible fare on the journeys performed
by airlines, other than Air India, may however be restricted to LTC fare being so charged
by Air India.
3.6 NORTH EASTERN REGION LIVELIHOOD PROJECT (NERLP)-EAP
RECOMMENDATION
3.6.1 The Committee notes the explanation and justification tendered by the Ministry about the
delay in the take off of the scheme. The scheme has been hanging fire for the last few years.
Nevertheless, the Committee hopes that the scheme would be implemented vigorously in the current
financial year. The Committee recommends that fool-proof arrangements for monitoring and
auditing of the scheme should be made, as an in-built mechanism, to plug leakage of funds
earmarked for improving living conditions of the poor. There should be no further delay in the
implementation of the scheme. (Para 2.13.6 ibid)
Action Taken
3.6.2 As per Project Implementation Plan (PIP) of NERLP, Monitoring and Evaluation would be
an inherent activity throughout the project cycle for feed-back on performance of the project
processes and activities. It is an important sub-component of Project Management. This involves
taking timely corrective measures to address the short comings and deviations. Monitoring and
Evaluation (M&E) system would provide realistic, real-time, adequately summarized and easily
interpretable information on various aspects of the project which would be helpful in its proper
implementation.
3.6.3 Objectives of this sub-component are:
1. To track the project input/output based on the project management matrix.
2. Collection and dissemination of information at the various levels for better planning and
implementation.
3.6.4 The Monitoring and Evaluation system of NERLP would cover the following broad activities:
• Progress monitoring of project inputs and outputs.
• Performance monitoring of community institutions, investments and project processes.
• Internal learning, feedback and social accountability measures
• Baseline and impact assessment
3.6.5 This sub-component will support project monitoring and learning activities, including
computerized Web-based MIS, baseline or end-line studies, mid-term review and impact studies.
The M&E system would monitor Processes, Results and Impact of various project initiatives. The

24
impact evaluation study would require rigorous methodology and quality analysis. Two impact
evaluations are planned during the project period. The mid-term evaluation would be commissioned
at the end of 3rd year of project intervention, while the final impact study would be conducted
at the end of the project period.
3.6.6 As per the Bye-Laws of the Society, C&AG shall audit the accounts of the society at least
once a year and annual Audit Report will be submitted to the Registrar of Societies regularly. The
Audit year of the Society shall begin on the first day of April and end on the 31st day of March
next year. The Society shall maintain proper accounts and other relevant records as well as
documents comprising of receipt and payment accounts, statement of assets and liabilities and
balance sheet. The accounts of the Society shall be audited by the C&AG .
3.6.7 The nature of the audit to be applied and the detail arrangement to be made in regard to
the account and their maintenance and the presentation of the accounts for audit shall be as per
the Auditing Standards promulgated by the C&AG guidelines. The auditor shall also submit a report
showing the exact state of financial affairs of the Society. The copies of the balance sheet and the
auditor’s report shall be certified by the auditor.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION
3.6.8 The Committee while noting the detailed arrangements for Monitoring and Auditing
of scheme under North Eastern Region livelihood project (NERLP) EAP for ensuring timely
implementation of the scheme. The Committee is of the view that the Project
Implementation Plan (PIP) of NERLP and the Monitoring and Evaluation system should have
provided conducive economic atmosphere for taking off of the scheme and timely
completion of the projects. Moreover, provision of by-laws of the society, C&AG should have
plugged leakages of funds earmarked for improving living conditions of the poor. However,
nothing as such has been reflected in the Action Taken Notes of the Ministry to give the
status of the scheme. The Committee would like to be apprised of present status of the
scheme.
3.7 CONNECTIVITY
RECOMMENDATION
3.7.1 The Committee is also disappointed to note that the region has very limited night landing
facilities at airports and as of now there are no takers for night aircraft operations despite night
landing approval given. The Committee does not understand the reasoning given. If the facility is
provided there will definitely be passengers. The Committee recommends that government should
persuade the airline operators to use night landing facility at airports. The Government may
consider providing incentives to them. (Para 3.2.9 ibid)
Action Taken
3.7.2 At present, there are night operations at Guwahati, Agartala and Imphal airports. Once the
hangars are commissioned then it is expected that the number of Night Landing Operations will
increase.
FURTHER RECOMMENDATION
3.7.3 The Committee is not happy with this vague reply. If hangars are required for Night

25
Landing Operation, then hangers may be provided the other airports also. Early steps may
be taken in this regard.
RECOMMENDATION
3.7.4 The Committee also recommends that steps may be taken for timely completion of all the
projects, particularly the projects which have been declared as National Projects. The Committee
desires that the works may be taken up on a fast track mode so that they are completed in time.
(Para 3.2.15 ibid)
Action Taken
3.7.5 Ministry of Railways are making concerted efforts for expeditious  completion of projects.
Status of various projects in the NE Region are as under:-
1. Jiribam-Tupul-Imphal (98 km.)
Status:
Project was initially sanctioned upto Tupul at a cost of Rs.727 crore in 2008-09, CCEA
approved extension of line upto Imphal with overall length as 125 km. Cost has gone up
substantially, primarily due to level difference between Tupul and Imphal necessitating
regarding of Jiribam-Imphal alignment involving 12.8 km. additional tunnelling. The present
estimated cost of the project is Rs.4444 crore. Final location survey in Tupal-Imphal section
has been completed. Land acquisition, earthwork, minor and major bridges and tunnel work
is in progress in Jiribam-Tupul section. 1089 hect. Out of 1282 hect. Land has been
acquired. 285 lac curn out of 515 lac cum earthwork and 33 out of 110 minor bridges have
been completed. Jiribam-Tupul section involves construction of 35 tunnels out of which
work has been commenced on 18 tunnels with total progress of 1.89 km.
Overall Physical Progress  : 20.73%
Target : Jiribam-Tupul : March, 2014
Tupul-Imphal : March, 2016
2. Rail-Cum-Road Bridge over river Brahmaputra near Bogibeel with linked lines on
North and South Bandh
Status:
The work of construction of Embarkment, Guide Bunds, Major and Minior bridges, station
works and raising and strengthening of Dykes on the North and South bank of bridge has
been completed. Chalkhowa-Moranhat rail link (44 km.) on South Bank completed and
commissioned on 08.12.2009.
On main bridge portion, 30 wall foundations and 14 piers out of 42 have been completed
and work is in progress on 7 walls and 10 piers. Contract for superstructure has been
recently awarded and agency is mobilizing resources. Progress of the project is frequently
disrupted due to militant/anti-social activities in the area, extortion demands by militants/anti-
social elements, disturbances at work sites and security threats to railway officials and
contractor personnel.
Overall Physical Progress : 75.39%
Target : Dec.,15

3.7.6 The Committee expresses its concern over the slow progress of  Railway Projects in
the North Eastern Region. Jiribam-Tupul-Imphal has achieved only 20.73% of physical
target while 24.61% of work is yet to be completed on Rail-Cum-Road Bridge over river
Brahmaputra near Bogibeel with linked lines on North and South Bandh. While the
Dimapur-Zubza (Kohima) New Line is at geographical survey stage, slow progess is being
observed at Tetlia-Byrnihat New Line and Bhairabhi-Sairang New Line. Only 34.49% of

Railways should analyse the situation and make all out efforts to clean the hurdles and
should not leave any stone unturned for ensuring timely completion of the projects so that
early Rail Linkages are provided to the people of North Eastern Region.

4.1 KEY AREAS AND PROJECTS UNDER LOOK EAST POLICY
RECOMMENDATION
4.1.1 Myanmar is an important neighbour which is strategically very crucial for the country, in
general, and North-east India, in particular. Strategic and trade links with Myanmar require
seamless flow of traffic between Myanmar and India. Keeping the Chinese presence in the region
in mind, such projects are of national importance. Besides, they can also be used for people-to-
people contacts in future, after Myanmar returns to full democracy. The Committee notes the
current status of the Kaladan Multi-model project and desires that the project may be completed
on schedule by July, 2013. The Committee recommends that the DPR to be prepared by the IRCON
for the entire road segment of project in Myanmar side be prepared as per schedule. The Committee
also recommends that the Government of Myanmar may be persuaded to construct the road as per
national highway standards. (Para 3.4.11 ibid)
4.1.2 Construction of Rhi-Tiddim and Rhi-Falam Roads are a case of improper handling. The
Committee is dismayed to note that the project of construction of Rhi-Tidim road had to be
revisited and the project was proposed to be assigned to IRCON along with updation of DPR, while
the project was earlier decided to be assigned to the Ministry of Construction of Myanmar, who
agreed to build two lane highway at the same cost, which was estimated by Border Road
Organization for a single lane highway. The Committee desires to know the reasons for this wide
difference in the costs quoted by both sides. The Committee during discussions on Demands for
Grant( 2010-11) was informed that the project would span over a period of three years i.e. till
2013. Now, in the present circumstances it is highly unlikely that the project will meet its deadline.
The Committee is extremely disappointed by the procedural delays, which reflect very poorly on the
seriousness with which the development of the region is taken by different Ministries/Departments.
(Para 3.4.12 ibid)
4.1.3 The committee hopes that the Government of Bangladesh will accept India’ s offer of
assistance for development of Ashuganj(Bangladesh) as port of call for the mutual benefit of both
countries. (Para 3.4.13 ibid)
4.1.4 The Committee is of the view that direct bus service between Kolkata and Dhaka will
benefit people of both the countries. The Committee recommends that all further necessary
diplomatic steps may be taken for early start of the bus service. (Para 3.4.14 ibid)
4.1.5 The Committee notes the typical bureaucratic style so far as dealing with the project on tri-
lateral highway connecting Moreh to Maesot (Thailand) is concerned in the light of the fact that
Thailand and Myanmar have started work on their parts of the project with their own resources,
while India is yet to take up the work. The Committee recommends that the Government may take
immediate steps in this regard. (Para 3.4.15 ibid)

of External Affairs, Ministry of Road Transport and Highways and Ministry of Home Affairs for
Action Taken Notes. Response of these Ministries are awaited.

I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home
Affairs, having been authorized by the Committee to submit the Report on its behalf, do hereby
present this One Hundred and Sixty Seventh Report on the Criminal Law (Amendment) Bill, 2012.

within three months.
3. The Bill seeks to substitute Sections 375, 376, 376A and 376B by replacing the existing
Sections 375, 376, 376A, 376B, 376C and 376D of Indian Penal Code, 1860, and replacing the
word ‘rape’ wherever it occurs by the word ‘sexual assault’ and make the offence of sexual

Bill proposes to make offence under Section 354 and 359 of IPC more stringent and also seeks
to amend Sections 154, 160, 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure 1973 for providing
protection to women and male person under the age of 18 years and above 65 years. The Bill
further aims to insert a new Section 53A in the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 wherein evidence of
the character of the victim or of his or her previous sexual experience shall not be relevant or

CHAPTER-I
BACKGROUND OF THE BILL
1.1 INTRODUCTION
1.1.1 According to the Statement of Objects and Reasons, the Criminal Law (Amendment) Bill,
2012 seeks to amend the Indian Penal Code, 1860, the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 and the
Indian Evidence Act, 1872. On the basis of the recommendations of the Law Commission of India
made in its One Hundred Seventy Second report on ‘Review of Rape Laws’ as well as the
recommendations of the National Commission for Women for providing stringent punishment for
the offence of rape, a High Power Committee (HPC) was constituted consisting of the
representatives of the Ministry of Women and Child Development, Ministry of Law and Justice,
National Commission for Women, Law Commission of India and the Ministry of Home Affairs to
examine the matter considering the suggestions of various quarters on the subject. The High Power
Committee submitted its report along with the draft Criminal Law (Amendment) Bill, 2011 and
recommended to the Government for its enactment.
1.1.2 The Bill seeks to achieve the following objectives :–
(a) Substitute Sections 375, 376, 376A and 376B by replacing the existing Sections 375,
376, 376A, 376B, 376C and 376D of the Indian Penal Code, and replacing the word
‘rape’ wherever it occurs by the words ‘sexual assault’, to make the offence of sexual
assault gender neutral and also widening the scope of the offence of sexual assault;
(b) Insert new Sections 326A and 326B in the Indian Penal Code to make acid attack a
specific offence;
(c) Enhance the punishment under Sections 354 and 509 of the Indian Penal Code, making
the offence more stringent;
(d) Amend Sections 154, 160 and 161 of the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973 for
providing male persons under the age of eighteen years or above the age of sixty-five
years and women more protection;
(e) Amend the Indian Evidence Act, 1872 by way of inserting a new Section 53A wherein
evidence of the character of the victim or of his or her previous sexual experience
shall not be relevant or questioned.
1.2 HISTORICAL BACKGROUND
1.2.1 According to the background note furnished by the Ministry of Home Affairs, in the year
1997, Sakshi (NGO), a non-governmental organization engaged in empowering women, filed a Writ
Petition in the Supreme Court of India seeking, inter alia , directions concerning definition of the
expression ‘sexual intercourse’ as contained in Section 375 of the Indian Penal Code, 1860
(hereinafter called IPC). The Supreme Court directed the Law Commission of India to file its
response with respect to the issue raised in the Writ Petition. The Commission filed an affidavit
in July 1998. The Supreme Court, however, directed Sakshi to draw a note containing the precise
issues involved in the petition and directed the Law Commission of India to examine the said issues

2
afresh. The Law Commission, in its 172 nd Report, made recommendation for widening the scope
of rape and to make it gender neutral.
1.2.2 The Ministry of Home Affairs in the background note further stated that since the Criminal
Law and the Criminal Procedure are in the Concurrent List of the Seventh Schedule to the
Constitution of India, the Report of the Law Commission was referred to the State Governments
for their views/comments. The State Governments were consulted on the recommendations made
by the Law Commission. Most of the State Governments supported the views of the Law
Commission. Thereafter, on the basis of the Law Commission’s Report, the Legislative Department
drafted a Bill. Meanwhile, the National Commission for Women (NCW) forwarded a separate Bill
on the same subject. Accordingly, the recommendations of the Law Commission of India, the draft
Bill prepared by the Legislative Department and the Bill forwarded by NCW were discussed by the
then Home Minister with the then Law Minister where the then Chairperson, National Commission
for Women was also present. It was stated that during the discussion, the view that emerged was
that various sexual offences specifically relating to males and females should be differentiated and
the crime should remain gender specific, and therefore, the recommendations of the Law
Commission would need a re-look taking into account the suggestions made by the National
Commission for Women.
1.2.3 The Ministry further stated in the background note that the Legislative Department,
accordingly, having regard to the sensitivity of the subject, was requested to revise the draft Bill
taking into consideration the above suggestions. It was also requested that the revised Bill should
address the existing inadequacies in the laws relating to sexual offences and also provide for
measures to deal with the sexual abuse of children through stringent provisions. Accordingly, the
Legislative Department prepared a revised Bill. The National Commission for Women recommended
some changes relating to ‘rape’ in its Annual Report 2004-05. Since the Criminal Law and the
Criminal Procedure are in the Concurrent List of the Seventh Schedule to the Constitution of India
and the laws are also being administered/implemented by the State Governments/Union Territory
Administrations, their views were sought on the recommendations made by the NCW in its
aforesaid Report. In order to get a quicker response, a Conference of the Home Secretaries of the
State Governments and Union Territory Administrations was convened on 7
th July, 2008 in Delhi
to discuss the matter relating to rape/sexual assault. There was no agreement as to the amendments
that should be carried out in IPC, Cr.P.C. and the Indian Evidence Act.
1.2.4 The Ministry of Home Affairs mentioned in its background note on the Bill that as the
subject matter relating to rape is sensitive in nature, it was decided that the Bill on rape laws may
be finalized after an in depth consultation with all concerned. Therefore, a High Powered
Committee (HPC) was constituted on 29
th January, 2010 under the Chairmanship of the former
Union Home Secretary comprising Secretary, Ministry of Women and Child Development;
Secretary, Department of Legal Affairs; Secretary, Legislative Department; Member Secretary,
NCW; Member Secretary, Law Commission of India; Special Secretary, MHA and Consultant
(Judl.), MHA as members to examine the issue relating to the review of rape laws. The HPC
discussed the matter in its meetings held on 12.2.2010 and 15.3.2010. The suggestions made by
the HPC were formulated into a draft Criminal Law (Amendment) Bill, 2010 which was referred
to the State Governments for their comments/views. The draft Bill was also posted on the website
of the Ministry of Home Affairs for comments of the general public. The HPC after going into the
comments received from the various individuals and NGOs, the State Governments and also after
further consultation amongst its members on 10.08.2010, 04.10.2010 and 08.02.2011 finalized its
report along with the draft Criminal Law (Amendment) Bill, 2011 and recommended to the
Government for its enactment.
1.2.5 The Committee was further apprised that the provisions of the draft Criminal Law
(Amendment) Bill, 2011 as formulated by the HPC were further examined in the Ministry of Home

3
Affairs in consultation with Legislative Department, Ministry of Law and Justice. After necessary
modifications, the Legislative Department provided a revised draft Criminal Law (Amendment) Bill,
2012. After consultation with other stake holders like Ministry of Law & Justice and Ministry of
Women & Child Development, a Cabinet Note on “Review of legal provisions pertaining to sexual
assault - Proposal to amend the Indian Penal Code, 1860, the Code of Criminal Procedure, 1973
and the Indian Evidence Act, 1872” was finalized and sent to the Cabinet for consideration on
02.07.2012. The Cabinet considered the note on 19.07.2012 and approved the proposal of
introduction of the Bill in the Parliament. Accordingly, the Bill was introduced in the Lok Sabha
on 04.12.2012.
1.3 FRESH DEVELOPMENT
1.3.1 A fresh development took place while the Committee was examining the Criminal Law
(Amendment) Bill, 2012. The President promulgated the Criminal Law (Amendment) Ordinance,
2013 on 3rd February, 2013. The Committee felt surprised on this development, because the Bill
was already before it for examination and report and the Parliament was to meet for the Budget
Session within a fortnight. The Committee also took into account some reports coming from
women organizations and other civil societies protesting against the said Ordinance on account of
not accepting the recommendations of the Justice Verma Committee in toto .
1.3.2 The Committee in its sitting held on 4
th February, 2013 wanted Home Secretary to explain
the circumstances which necessitated the Government to issue this Criminal Law (Amendment)
Ordinance, 2013.
Responding to the Committee’s query, Home Secretary replied as under:–
“in the last meeting, agreed that the Committee would give holistic recommendations which
take into account both the provisions in the Bill as introduced in the House as also the
recommendations of the Verma Committee. Sir, there has been no departure from that stand.
The Government sticks to that stand. Therefore, the Government’ s request would be that the
Committee should go into the Bill, the Ordinance and the other recommendations of the
V erma Committee which are not included in the Ordinance, or any other provision which
the Committee feels appropriate to have in a Bill of this nature. When the Committee gives
its recommendations, then the Government will have the benefit of its advice over the whole
gamut of issues. Then, I think, we can bring in amendments which are comprehensive in
nature, covering every aspect.”
1.3.3 The Committee sought to know whether the Committee could discuss the Ordinance.
Responding to that the Home Secretary replied as under:
“...my submission is that this Committee is entirely within its powers to take into account
any existing laws or proposed laws or any Ordinance or any other material which will have
a bearing on this subject. Therefore, the Committee will be very much within its rights to
go into the Ordinance as well. But, the Ordinance has two parts... the Ordinance is made
up of the provisions which were there in the Criminal Law (Amendment) Bill and the
provisions which are there in the Verma Committee Report. Some provisions of the Verma
Committee Report are not there in the Ordinance; otherwise the Ordinance is only comprised
of these two. ... if you cover the Criminal Law (Amendment) Bill and you cover the Verma
Committee Report, then, I think the whole gamut in any case would be covered. ..., as I
said, the Committee will be within its rights to take into account any material which has
a bearing on this subject.”
1.3.4 In the meeting of the Committee held on 11
th February, 2013, the Chairman informed the
Members that sub rule (2) of Rule 66 of the Rules of Procedure and Conduct of Business in the

4
Rajya Sabha envisages a situation where an Ordinance can be promulgated to enforce the
provisions of a Bill which is pending before the Council. Identical rule also exists in Rules of
Procedure and Conduct of Business in the Lok Sabha.
1.3.5 The Chairman further stated that he has been given to understand that there had been

1998, the High Court and Supreme Court Judges (Salaries and Conditions of Service) Amendment

1.3.6 The Chairman then informed the Members that in the light of the above, he feels that the
