Corporation is projecting internal generation of around Rs. 300 crore, market borrowing of Rs. 90
Crore and soft loan of Rs. 60 Crore from the Ministry of DoNER.
2.8.4 The Ministry also informed that in the financial year 2011-12, NEDFi has sanctioned an
amount of Rs.432.23 crore covering 253 projects and during financial year 2012-13, the sanctioned
amount is expected to touch Rs.450 crore spread over all the eight States of North-East India. The
total disbursement for the year 2011-12 was Rs.334.56 Crore whereas during FY 2012-13 as on
date, the amount disbursed is Rs.255.00 crore which is expected to touch Rs.350 crore at the end
of the financial year.
2.8.5 During the last two years, under its microfinance scheme, NEDFi has sanctioned and
disbursed an amount of Rs.127.29 crore. and Rs.118.94 crore respectively. The cumulative
sanction and disbursement are Rs.229 crore and Rs.214 crore, respectively. NEDFi has identified
the Micro and Small Enterprises (MSE) Sector, especially to help the first generation
entrepreneurs, as its priority sector for assistance. The Corporation has designed several need
based schemes (specific to certain sectors and certain categories) like NEDFi Opportunity
Scheme for Small Enterprise (NOSSE), North East Entrepreneurs Development Scheme
(NEEDS), Women Enterprise Development Scheme (WEDS), Scheme for Northeast Handloom
and Handicrafts (SNEHH), Jute Enterprise Development Scheme (JEDS), Initiative for
Development of Entrepreneurs in Agriculture (IDEA), etc. The Corporation is also giving top
priority to micro finance to bring micro-credit to the grass root level in the rural areas as well
as the unserved and underserved hill areas. In terms of Industries, several industries like
infrastructure, power, hospitality, healthcare, food processing, higher education, etc. has been
identified as the priority sectors for assistance.

19
2.8.6 On being enquired as to how this Corporation identifies the units which are in need of
finance and how far it has been successful in terms of financing industrial, infrastructural and
agro-horticultural projects in the region, the Ministry informed that the identification of need for
finance is done either through receipt of enquires from walk-in customers at the Corporation’s head
office in Guwahati or through its 14 Branch offices located at Agartala, Aizawl, Dharmanagar,
Dimapur, Gangtok, Imphal, Itanagar, Kohima, Lunglei, Namchi, Shillong, Silchar, Tinsukia and
Udaipur. Other points of contact are five Representative Offices located in Assam (Kokrajhar,
Goalpara, Sibsagar), Manipur (Churachanpur), and Meghalaya (Tura).
2.8.7 Besides walk-in customers, the Corporation also conducts Investor Meets, Workshops and
Entrepreneurship Development Programmes (EDPs) all over North-Eastern Region for dissemination
of information on schemes and programmes of the Corporation. In addition, for first generation
entrepreneurs, business facilitation programmes are held at specific locations. These Seminars,
Workshops and EDPs also become a contact point for identifying the financing needs of the
entrepreneurs.
2.8.8 Since its inception NEDFi has financed industrial and infrastructure projects like Steel
Re-rolling Mills, Cement plants, Ferro-Alloy manufacturing units, Captive Power Plants, Contract
Financing in construction of roads and railway tunneling works, Hospitals/ Nursing Homes, Hotels/
Resorts, Educational Institutes, etc. Over the years, NEDFi has been able to mobilize capital
investment of more than Rs. 10000 Crore by sanctioning 2892 projects with loan amount of
Rs. 2844 crore (as on 28.02.2013). More than 28000 employment opportunities have been created
in the Region with the organization’s direct assistance scheme.
2.8.9 The Corporation was initially set up exclusively for support of industrial and infrastructure
projects in the NE Region. However, keeping in view the agro-horticulture potential in the Region,
the same was brought under the mandate of NEDFi in the year 2000. A total of Rs. 212.40 crore
has been sanctioned by the Corporation since 2005-06 for agro based industries, horticultural
projects and food processing industries covering 300 projects. The projects assisted by the
Corporation includes tea processing unit, cold storage, dairy farm, milk processing unit, bamboo
and wood based industries, rubber based industries, fruit processing unit, beverages, medicinal and
aromatic oil processing units, piggery, poultry, etc.
2.8.10 About gender budgeting and budgeting for the economically and socially weaker sections, the
Ministry informed that the gender perspective has been kept in mind and schemes have been
exclusively designed to suit the needs of the north east women. Development of entrepreneurship as
well as encouragement of income generating activities among grass-root women is a major focus area
of the Corporation’s operation. To provide assistance exclusively to women entrepreneurs for taking
up business ventures, the corporation has developed a scheme, Women Enterprise Development
Scheme (WEDS). Under the scheme, assistance up to 75% of the project cost is funded at the
subsidized interest rate of 8 per cent p.a. for new/expansion projects with a maximum project cost
of Rs. 15 lakh for income generating activities like handloom and handicrafts, dairy farming, poultry,
grocery shops, small restaurants and tea shops, etc. Under this scheme, so far NEDFi has assisted
991 women entrepreneurs all over North-Eastern Region, which is more than one-third of the total
project assisted by the Corporation so far. The cumulative amount sanctioned and disbursed under
the scheme is Rs. 2476 lakh and Rs. 2211 lakh, respectively.
2.8.11 Besides the above scheme, NEDFi also has a very successful Micro finance scheme where
assistance is provided through NGOs for on-lending to the underprivileged sections of the society
all over the NE Region for taking up income generating activities like weaving, tailoring, trading,
goat rearing, poultry etc. The total number of beneficiaries under this programme has reached more
than 310,000, out of which more than 283,000 beneficiaries are women (over 90 percent). The
total numbers of SC and ST beneficiaries are more than 25,000 and 51,000 respectively.

20
2.8.12 Under another special micro finance scheme designed for Women beneficiaries of Backward
Classes, the Corporation has disbursed Rs. 1650 lakh to 16,180 OBC beneficiaries, all women
beneficiaries, getting assistance at 4% (NEDFi lends to NGOs/MFIs at 2%).
2.8.13 NEDFi is also conducting design and skill upgradation programmes on regular basis to
provide new designs, avenues for product diversification, upgrading skills of the artisans,
introducing better production techniques, providing linkages to improve margins and incomes and
also capacity building for credit linkages. Under this programme, 2236 weavers and artisans (out
of which around three-fourth were women) have received training in 83 programmes all over the
NE. The Ministry also informed that the Corporation has put in place the policy guidelines for
rehabilitation of sick units. Besides, 198 potentially sick units have been restored to health through
loan restructuring/rephasement.
2.8.14 North Eastern Development Finance Corporation Limited (NEDFi) is an extremely
important Institution of the NER which provides term finance to industry, agro-horticulture
based industries and infrastructure along with services to the small entrepreneurs of the
region.The Committee has been informed that the Corporation is projecting internal
generation of around Rs. 300 crore, market borrowing of Rs. 90 crore and soft loan of
Rs. 60 crore from the Ministry of DoNER during the financial year 2013-14. The Committee
notes that though the Corporation has a target of 25-30 per cent growth on year-on-year
basis but it has scaled down its disbursement target from RS. 485.00 crore during the
financial year 2012-13 to Rs. 450 crore during the financial year 2013-14  due to resource
constraints. The Committee, therefore, recommends that adequate fund may be provided to
NEDFi at RE stage to carry out its activities as projected.
2.8.15 The Committee is given to understand that the corporation has fund requirement
of Rs. 5184 crore during the Twelfth Five Year Plan to meet the projected sanctions of
Rs. 6410.00 crore and disbursement of Rs. 4690.00 crore. The corporation has further
requested for interest-free loan to the tune of Rs. 1000.00 crore from the Government
during Twelfth Five Year Plan. Keeping in view the pivotal role of NEDFi, the Committee
reiterates its recommendation made in its 162nd Report on Demands for Grants (2012-13)
of the Ministry  that the Government should consider interest-free loan to the tune of
Rs. 1000.00 crore for ensuring NEDFi to meet its financial and physical targets during the
Twelfth Five Year Plan.

2.9.13 Regarding the criteria for deciding the quantum of grants given to the States from Central
Pool of Resources, the Ministry informed that the  Funds allotted to North Eastern States under

on the basis of latest data available.

creates hurdles in the way of fresh allocation from the Pool for projects which, in turn,
delays the completion of projects causing time and cost overruns. The Committee urges
upon the State Governments concerned to submit Utilization Certificates on time so that
funds could be released on time and delays could be avoided.

CHAPTER-III
Issues, Schemes, Policies and Programmes
3.1 WORKING/MANDATE OF THE MINISTRY OF DoNER
3.1.1 The Committee has been informed that the primary role of the Ministry of DoNER is limited
to advocacy to stimulate planning and facilitate and accelerate projects/scheme implementation in
NER, but the main problem faced by the Ministry is its weaknesses inherent in any advocacy and
coordination role. The Committee has also been informed that it faces problems of inadequate
technical support, inadequate overall support, inadequate space and lack of field offices.
3.1.2 The Committee fails to understand that a Ministry, which was carved out to focus
and expedite development in the North east region, after more than a decade of its
existence has realized that it lacks sufficient power and necessary infrastructure to carry
out its mandate, and is completely dependent on various Line Ministries/Departments for
execution of projects. The Committee takes a serious view of the situation and feels that
a holistic view at the functioning and powers of the Ministry should be taken at this stage.
The Committee is not at all impressed with the functioning of the Ministry and gets an
impression that the line ministries are not supporting or paying heed to the suggestions/
requests of the ministry. The Committee intends to discuss this issue separately at a later
stage with all stakeholders and authorities. The Committee therefore recommends that the
Ministry should furnish a detailed note, based on the last 12-13 years of experience
indicating about the bottlenecks and shortcomings and the desired solutions. The Committee
also proposes to discuss the matter with the Cabinet Secretary and Secretaries of all the
line Ministries and the Chief Secretaries of the State Governments  so as to enable the
Ministry to effectively tackle the issues faced it. The Committee also intends to discuss with
the Planning Commission about the need for reviewing all the schemes being implemented
in the North East to have a holistic view in the matter and also to find solutions to the
problems faced by the Ministry.
3.2 INFRASTRUCTURAL PROJECTS
3.2.1 The Committee was given to understand that cost of construction in NER projects is
invariably high in comparison to similar projects in rest of the country and delays in execution of
infrastructural projects in NER are also common. Limitations and challenges for implementation of
infrastructure projects in NER are many, viz.  limited working season, difficulty in getting
environment and forest clearances, especially in view of Forest Rights Act, 2006, non-availability
of experienced contractors, deficiency in capacities of Government executing agencies, law &
order problems, non-availability of building materials in the Region etc.
3.2.2 The Ministry has informed that it has taken several initiatives with Ministries/Departments
concerned like holding regular coordination meetings on major infrastructure projects, capacity
building of State Governments’ executing agencies, follow up action with MoEF for forest
clearances etc. The issue of land acquisition for infrastructure projects is challenging, especially in
view of provisions of Forest Rights Act, 2006. All environment and forest clearances for these
projects require ‘No Objection’ from concerned authorities and evidence of consent of the Gram
Panchayats.

33
3.2.3 The Ministry has informed that it takes up the review with the Project Implementation
Authorities, State Governments, Central Ministries/Departments of all NER infrastructure projects.
Regular coordination meetings of stakeholders are held to facilitate identification of problem areas
and steps are taken to resolve them. NE States mostly do not have their digitized land records and
in many States, the cadastral survey of their land has not been done. Under such situation, the
village councils consent is sought as per provisions of Forest Rights Act, 2006. As these are
statutory provisions applicable for almost all projects, delays become unavoidable. Hence, Ministry
of DoNER is developing standard procedures to be followed in such cases and strengthening them.
3.2.4 The Committee is extremely concerned about abnormally long delays taking place in
execution of infrastructure projects in the Region. The Committee observes that the
Ministry comes up with similar alibis every time whenever they are asked about the delays.
The Committee, while acknowledging the fact that the region suffers from peculiar
problems, feels that a way out has to be found out, because neither the climate of the
region is going to change nor the region can be allowed to lag behind on the pretext of
adverse circumstances. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should look for
various technological interventions such as pre-fabricated structures, other innovative
methods and digitization of land records among others to speed up the process of project
execution.
3.3 POTENTIAL OF HYDRO-ELECTRIC (HE) PRODUCTION IN NE REGION
3.3.1 The Committee is aware of the fact that NE Region has enormous hydro-electricity
generation potential. Based on the studies for re-assessment of hydro-electric potential of the
country by Central Electricity Authority in 1987, the identified potential of 58356 MW in NE Region
constitutes about 40.1% of the total identified hydro power potential of 145320 MW in the country.
The Ministry has informed that a capacity of 1200 MW has so far been harnessed in NE region
(2.06% of the identified capacity) while 6 HE projects with aggregate capacity of 2852 MW
(4.89%) are under construction in NER.
3.3.2 The Committee was also informed that a number of policy measures have been taken by
the Government in the past to give the thrust to the development of the hydro electric potential
in the region. These include:
(a) Policy Liberalisation for encouraging Private Sector Participation
(b) Policy on Hydro Power Development, 2008
(c) National Water Policy, 2002
(d) Electricity Act, 2003
(e) National Electricity Policy  announced by Government in Feb.’2005
(f) National Policy on Rehabilitation and Resettlement, 2007 in order to protect the
interests of affected persons
3.3.3 The Committee was apprised by the Ministry that to expedite development of balance hydro
electric projects in the country, a large number of projects have been allotted/identified by various
States for implementation in Private, Central and State Sector during Twelfth Plan period and
beyond. This included 138 projects (above 25 MW capacity) aggregating to 56063 MW of capacity
for implementation in NE Region. Out of these, 98 schemes with aggregate capacity of 34434.5 MW
have been allotted to private sector while 11 with an aggregate capacity of 8247 MW have been
allotted to CPSUs. The remaining schemes are either to be implemented in State Sector or are yet
to be allotted.

34
3.3.4 An Inter-Ministerial Group (IMG) had been constituted by Ministry of Water Resources
(MoWR) on 7th August, 2009 under the Chairmanship of Secretary, Water Resource on the
directions of Prime Minister’s Office (PMO) to evolve a suitable framework to guide and accelerate
the development of Hydro power in the North East which identified major issues/ constraints in
the way of expeditious growth of hydro power development in the Region and proposed a number
of policy interventions.
3.3.5 The Ministry further informed that for monitoring of the ongoing hydro projects, a task
force has been constituted under the Chairmanship of Minister of Power with Deputy Chairman,
Planning Commission, Minister of Water Resources, Minister of New and Renewable Energy,
Minister of Environment and Forest and Ministers of Power from Hydro rich States in order to
look into all issues relating to development of Hydro Power including issues of rehabilitation and
resettlement of project affected persons. In addition, an Advisory Group has been set up under the
chairmanship of the Minister of Power to advise for expeditious completion of ongoing power
generation projects. Further, a Special Monitoring Group (SMG) under the chairmanship of
Secretary (Power) has been constituted to discuss and sort out various issues through video
conferencing for J&K and North Eastern Region.
3.3.6 Following mechanism is also in place to monitor the progress of projects under
construction:
• In pursuance of Section 73 (f) of Electricity Act, 2003, Central Electricity Authority
(CEA) is performing the duties (monitoring of the power projects). The progress of
each project is monitored continuously through frequent site visits, interaction with the
developers, and critical study of monthly progress reports. Chairperson, CEA holds
review meeting with the developers and other stakeholders to sort out the critical
issues.
• A Power Project Monitoring Panel (PPMP) has been set up by the Ministry of Power
to independently follow up and monitor the progress of the hydro projects.
• Review meetings are taken by Ministry regularly with the concerned officers of CEA,
equipment manufacturers, State Utilities/CPSUs/Project developers, etc.
3.3.7 The Committee is at a loss to understand that despite such elaborate planning and
huge administrative mechanism, the realization of the potential remains abysmally low. The
Committee finds that even though Inter-Ministerial Groups (IMG), Task Force, Advisory
Groups and Special Monitoring Groups (SMG) were set up by the Government at one point
of time or other to sort out the problems afflicting the projects, yet perceptible outcome is
still a distant dream.
3.3.8 The Committee finds that while the identified potential in NE Region constitutes
about 40.1% of the total identified hydro power potential (145320 MW) in the country, but
only 1200 MW has so far been harnessed in NE region which is 2.06% of the identified
capacity and only 6 HE projects with aggregate capacity of 2852 MW (4.89%) are under
construction in NER. Even if the under construction projects in the region are completed on
time, the potential likely to be realized will only be close to 7%. This leaves a huge gap
between potential capacity and potential realized. In an energy deficit country like ours, this
is totally unacceptable. The Committee feels that the huge bureaucratic mechanism put in
place for the purpose and the policy guidelines adopted by themselves are not enough and
a spirited effort is required to make things happen on the ground. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that a very practical approach with quantifiable progress indicators
should be adopted for progress on ground.

35
3.3.9 The Committee feels that the Ministry of DoNER must play pro-active coordinating
role and act in tandem with Ministry of Water Resources, Power, Forest and Environment
and concerned State Governments in NER to harness Hydro power potential optimally.
3.3.10 The Committee has been informed that Rs. 90 crore have been spent on Centrally-sponsored
Dimapur Power Project and the project has been abandoned. This was brought to the notice of
the Committee of Secretaries headed by the Cabinet Secretary. The recommendation of the
Committee of Secretaries was that the land acquired for the project and the civil structure be
utilized by the State Government and the equipment procured for the project may be auctioned by
the State Government in consultation with BHEL. The matter is under active consideration of the
State Government and BHEL. It will be done shortly.
3.3.11 The Committee is extremely disappointed to note that Dimapur Power Project has
been abandoned after spending an amount of Rs. 90 crore. The Committee observes that
money spent on the project and subsequently abandoned, reflects lack of proper planning
and is a criminal wastage of fund. The Committee is of the considered opinion that the
project should have been more carefully planned and executed avoiding huge waste of
precious resources.
3.3.12 Regarding the Lower Subansiri Project, the downstream areas of Assam have been agitating
stating concerns about dam safety and on the variation in flow that is likely to result once the
project comes into existence. Several Committees were set up on various aspects of the project.
The Ministry has also been conducting talks with various stakeholders and civil society groups
alongside. The  Ministry has informed that by the  end of April, when  the final recommendations
on the dam safety is available with the Ministry, they  would put all of them together and have
a final meeting with the Government of Assam to arrive at the steps to be taken to take care of
all the concerns.
3.3.13 The Committee has been informed that around Rs. 6,000 crore have already been spent on
the project and the estimated completion cost has gone upto Rs. 11,000 crore. The Committee has
also been informed that for every month of delay, the Government is losing Rs. 60 crore.
3.3.14 The Committee is astonished to find that on Lower Subansiri Project the estimated
completion cost has gone upto Rs. 11,000 crore and Government is losing Rs. 60 crore  for
every month of delay due to the concerns of the people over the Dam safety. The
Committee recommends that the  Ministry after receiving the recommendations on Dam
safety should attempt to win the confidence of the affected people by proper counselling so
that  the project takes off at the earliest. The Committee also hopes that once the project
gets started, the Ministry would ensure that the project is completed without further delay
and cost escalation.

3.6 The Ministry also informed  about the steps it has taken to expedite the Railway projects
suffering from the following obstacles:
3.6.1 Limited working season from November to March
Due to restricted working season in North East, efforts are being made to start the work

3.6.2 Militant activity and prevailing security scenario in North East Region
Law and order is a State subject and wherever environment is not conducive for execution
of projects, State Government/MHA are requested to provide adequate security at project sites. In
some of the projects such as Lumding-Silchar gauge conversion, dedicated battalions of Territorial
Army have been created chargeable to project for ensuring adequate security at work site.
3.6.3 Delay in land transfer to the project from State Government
Land acquisition in most of the projects is done by State Governments on behalf of
Railways. Regular meetings/correspondences are held with State Governments for expeditious
acquisition of land. Acquisition of land for some projects has also been taken up as Special Railway
Projects under Railway Amendment Act, 2008.
3.6.4 Forest clearance for Land
To expedite forestry clearance, Railways make all efforts to comply observations/objections
raised by M/o Environment Regular meetings are being held at higher level and Railway’s case is
adequately represented for early forestry clearance. Projects pending on account of forestry
clearance are also monitored at highest level in Cabinet Secretariat.
3.6.5 The Committee observes that several railway projects in NER suffer due to various
peculiarities viz., paucity of funds, limited working season, Militant activity and prevailing
security scenario in North East Region, delay in land transfer to the project from State
Government and Forest clearance for Land. The Committee believes that such limiting
factors should not discourage the concerned line Ministry from extending its concerted
attention towards development of the region. The Committee, has, therefore, recommended
on several occasions that the best way to adhere is to properly plan and make strategy for
development keeping in view the limiting factors so that any development project is not
held up halfway. The Committee is of the view that the stumbling bloc such as limited
working season can be tackled by customized technological solutions while administrative
problems like forest clearances and land acquisition on time could be resolved by better
coordination and persuasion at highest level.

42
3.6.6 The Committee understands that militant activity and prevailing security scenario is,
of course, a larger problem which requires a national level brain-storming exercise and
towards that direction, the Union Ministry of Home Affairs and concerned State Government
should take appropriate steps together in a coordinated way.
3.6.7 The Committee, therefore,  strongly recommends that the Ministry of Railway
should leave no stone unturned for timely augmentation of  railway network i.e. 13 new
lines, 4 gauge conversion and 1 doubling projects which have been taken up presently.

3.8 INLAND WATER CONNECTIVITY
3.8.1 Inland Waterways Authority of India (IWAT) is improving the Inland Waterways to provide
alternate connectivity within the NER and between the NER with the rest of the country. The
Ministry has provided details of progress in development of inland waterways in NE-Region as
given below:
A. National Waterway-2.
To develop Inland Water transport in North East, River Brahmaputra from Bangladesh
Border (near Dhubri) to Sadiya (891 km.) was declared as National Waterway No.2 in 1988.
Inland Waterways Authority of India, a statutory Body of Ministry of Shipping, is carrying
out various developmental works like navigable fairway, day and night navigation aids and
terminals etc. since then as briefed below:
(i) Fairway development works/ River conservancy works:
A navigable fairway of 45 meter width and 2.5 meter Least Available Depth (LAD) from
Bangladesh Border (Dhubri) to Neamati (630 km.), 2.0 meter from Neamati to Dibrugarh
(139 km.) and with 1.5 meter from Dibrugarh to Oriumghat (92 km.) is being developed
and maintained by undertaking annual river conservancy works like dredging. Till 2009-10,
IWAI was developing the navigational channel with 2.0 meter LAD in the entire waterway
which has been increased to 2.5 meter LAD in about 630 km. stretch now providing
increased viability for transportation by bigger cargo vessels. The dredging is carried out
with three departmental dredgers. Two more dredgers are planned to be deployed on this
waterway.
(ii) T erminals:
(a) Pandu IWT terminal with multi modal transit system : Pandu is the most important
location on NW-2 for development of river port. An amount of Rs. 95 crore has been
invested for construction of a low level jetty, a high level jetty (nearing completion) and
Railway BG siding. The port is being developed as a multi-modal modern Inland Water
Transport Terminal equipped with cargo handling facilities, transit sheds, appropriate open
space facilities/hard stands and rail and road connectivity. An alternate approach road for
movement of Heavy/Container Traffic connecting NH-31 at a cost of Rs. 11 crore has also
been approved and the work has been awarded to State PWD (NH Division). However,
construction could not be commenced as the land through which the alignment passes, is
yet to be handed over by NF Railway.
(b) Roll on-Roll off terminals: At Dhubri and Hatsingimari (opposite bank of Brahmaputra
at Dhubri), permanent terminals with Roll on-Roll off (Ro-Ro) facilities are proposed to be
established for which projects have been approved at an estimated cost of Rs. 31.80 crore
and Rs. 35.57 crore respectively by IWAI based on the detailed project reports prepared
through M/s L&T- ECC Chennai. Land has been acquired at both the locations and work
for construction of these terminals has been awarded to CPWD on 18.01.2013. Once these

44
terminals are constructed, there will be a direct link between Assam and Meghalaya across
the Brahmaputra through IWT avoiding circuitous route through Jogighopa. The work at
Dhubri will be commenced shortly. At Hatsingimari, severe erosion has been noticed and
work will commence after implementation of anti-erosion works by Brahmaputra Board.
B. Central Sector Plan Scheme for development of IWT infrastructure by the States of
NER:
Under a new Central Sector Scheme for NER for IWT sector (made operational from
August 2008), 100% grant is being provided by the Ministry of Shipping for development of Inland
Water transport projects in North Eastern States of the Country. Presently, following two projects
are under implementation under this scheme;
1. Mizoram: Development of Inland Water Transport in Tlawng River at a cost of
Rs.527.93 lakhs. (Completed recently)
2. Assam: Construction of 17M long floating terminals at 20 ghat on the river
Brahmaputra at a cost of Rs. 450.08 lakhs.
3.8.2 The Ministry has informed that keeping in view the poor response of NE States for
development of IWT projects, IWAI took the initiative for identification of IWT projects having
IWT potential in NE States and conducted a study through M/s RITES which identified 22 rivers

Tripura:  The project for “Preparation of DPR for development of Howrah River and Gumti

Meghalaya : The project for “Preparation of DPR for development of Inland Water

3.8.3 The Committee understands the importance of Inland Waterways as an alternative
to other modes of transport which are found lacking in many parts of the region. Inland
waterways  has huge potential which can also be used to supplement the existing routes on
land. Waterways are the cheapest mode of transport anywhere in the world. In Western

45
European countries, about 40 per cent of the cargo movement is by waterways. The world’s
average is about 8 per cent, whereas in India it is less than 1 per cent. The Committee is
surprised to find that in the National Water Policy, navigation comes almost towards the end
on the list of priority. The Committee, therefore, recommends that navigation in NER
should find priority as it is not only an economical mode of transport but also eco-friendly
and there is immense scope for improvement in the field of Inland Waterways in NER. The
Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the Ministry of Shipping along with
Ministry of Water Resources should pursue all the projects vigorously in close coordination
with the Ministry of DoNER. The Committee also recommends that fund constraints should
not come in the way of the implementation of projects. The Committee also recommends
that Inland Water Transport projects in Tripura, Meghalaya and Mizoram which are at
various stages of planning may be expedited and finalised.
3.8.4 The Committee notes with disappointment that Inland Waterway Terminal of Pandu
which is being developed as multi modal transit system is still hanging fire for want of
handing over of  land. The Committee directs that the matter should be taken up with the
NF Railway and resolved as soon as possible. The Committee further recommends that work
on proposed roll on-roll off terminals  at Dhubri and Hatsingimari be started immediately
without further delay. CPWD may take up the work on priority.

3.10 INDUSTRIAL SECTOR
3.10.1 The Committee believes that the main strength of the North Eastern Region for industrial
development emanates from its natural resource base. The huge hydro-electric potential has been
assessed. Minerals like oil, gas and limestone have long been used to feed various industries and
there is scope for further use of such resources for industrial use. Forest and bio-diversity can
be the resource base for developing industries in the region in future. Besides, the tea industry
continues to be a major strand in the region’s industrial set up. Processing of rubber and high value
horticulture crops can also emerge as important industrial activity once the agriculture sector of
the region gets commercialised and diversified.
3.10.2 The Committee further understands that traditional handicrafts skills of the people of the
region is yet another resource with potential for supporting considerable industrial employment once
the highly acclaimed tourism potential of the region is harnessed. However, in spite of being
endowed with vast natural resources in terms of forests, biological diversity, hydro-electricity, the
region has remained largely underdeveloped. A key constraint to the growth has been poor
infrastructure and limited connectivity, both within the region as well as with the rest of the
country.
3.10.3 The Committee has been apprised of the SWOT analysis of the industrial situation in NER
as under:
Strength
• Natural Resources.
• High level of literacy.

47
• Comparatively low cost of real estate.
• Availability of Inland water transportation.
3.10.4 Against the advantage of natural resource base, the major hindrances for industrial
development of the region appear to be:
Weaknesses
• Low productivity.
• Lack of skilled manpower.
• Lack of entrepreneurship.
• Low level of savings and investments.
• High freight cost.
• Isolation and inadequate linkage with the national economy.
• Dependence on other parts of the country for day to day consumption goods.
• Inadequate marketing initiatives.
Opportunities
• Setting up of processing units and industries based on locally available resources.
• Setting up of downstream units for oil industries.
• Cross-border trade with neighbouring countries.
• Possibilities of plantation and processing of aromatic/medicinal plants.
• Developing SMEs for producing items currently procured from other parts of the
country.
• Abundant possibilities for taking up tourism activities in the region.
• Government initiatives for development of NER.
Threat
• Law and order situation.
• Natural Calamities.
3.10.5 The Committee takes into account the SWOT analysis of  the industrial situation
in NER and views that the Ministry of DoNER should make a detailed analysis of the same
to take up the issue of the industrial development in NER with the concerned line
Ministries/Departments. The Committee recommends that the following prospects of
industrial development in NER must be harnessed for ensuring balanced regional
development:–
• The crude oil production and its refining as well as tea plantation and bamboo/
cane industries are the few resource-based industries in the region.
• Exploitation of the large hydro potential in the NER could be used for exporting
to the power deficit northern and western regions of the country.

48
• The Region’s comparative advantages in producing fruits, vegetables and other
horticulture products like spices can be tapped by setting up small-scale
processing units for the local market which would also boost rural employment.
• The North-East is an ideal destination for adventure, leisure and eco-tourism.
The mineral-rich north-eastern States can also explore and promote geo-tourism.
• The education sector in the North-East has emerged as a major destination for
private firms. To explore the opportunities available, several private players are
now targeting the region to set up educational institutions which would serve the
cross-country market and cater to the needs of neighbouring countries.
• The North-Eastern Region is an ideal destination for Information Technology,
specifically for ITES sector. IT enabled service coupled with BPO business are
other areas which have enormous scope to flourish in the North–Eastern Region
because it has an advantage in its English speaking population and proficiency/
efficiency acknowledged by captains of IT industries outside the NER. This
should be explored to the full potential.
• Prospects for investors from outside the Region for setting up of industrial units
taking advantage of the incentives provided under NEIIPP–2007 by the Ministry
of Commerce and Industry.
• Since North-East is located at a crossroads between three major economies –
East Asia, South Asia and Southeast Asia, with the implementation of the ‘Look
East policy’ and opening up of trade routes, processing industries manufacturing
quality products, can be offered in international markets at competitive prices.
3.10.6 The Committee believes that the spill-over benefits of industrial development for the
region would be the development of infrastructure such as roads, communications, and
electricity supply to remote hilly areas, resulting in better quality of life. Natural gas based
industries are also feasible. The Committee also believes that NER could be an excellent
centre for horticulture, spices, and hub for educational and IT sector.
3.10.7 Since  the region is expected to be declared as SEZ, there is every reason for the
Committee  to conclude that once the region is declared a SEZ by the Government of India,
there  would automatically come about a wide range of infrastructural development and a
rapid change in the industrial sector, opening scope for a rapid change in the socio-economic
scenario in the NE States. The Committee believes that industrial development can be made
in the NE States at par with the development in other regions of the country if all the steps
are taken in right ernest. The Committee recommends that the Government should make
concerted efforts in this direction.
3.10.8 The Committee was also informed that growth of Micro, Small and  Medium Enterprise
(MSMEs) in the NER is slow in comparison to the other parts of the country and at a very nascent
stage. Most of the States of NER are rich in natural endowment and the available resources can
be effectively utilised for growth of micro or small enterprises. The MSEs of the Region are
plagued by myriad problems which inter-alia  include high level of sickness in this sector,
inadequate infrastructure, poor connectivity and inaccessibility due to difficult terrain, inadequate
power supply, law and order, natural calamities – Floods, landslides, etc., lack of entrepreneurship,
low level of public sector investment, low productivity, lack of skilled manpower,  low level of
savings and investments, high freight cost, isolation and inadequate linkage with the national
economy, dependence on other parts of the country for day to day consumption goods and
Inadequate marketing initiatives.

49
3.10.9 The Committee is of the firm opinion that simultaneous growth of Micro, Small and
Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) along with big Business Enterprises can create an overall
growth story. Unfortunately the development pattern of the MSMEs of the Region is far
from encouraging.  The Committee is of the firm view that the growth of MSMEs touches
more directly, the lives of common people and can raise their income levels much more
drastically. The Committee therefore, strongly recommends that Government must address
the problems being faced by the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise (MSMEs).
3.11 EDUCATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES IN THE REGION.
3.11.1 The Committee notes that in the absence of availability of adequate educational
opportunities in the region, students belonging to the region have to go to far flung areas
of the country. The Committee urges the Ministry of HRD to explore ways and means to
provide such opportunities in the NE Region establishing more institutes and provide
adequate number of faculty positions.

OBSERV ATIONS/CONCLUSIONS/RECOMMENDATIONS OF THE COMMITTEE —
AT A GLANCE
PROJECTED DEMAND IN THE BUDGET 2013-14
The Committee notes with concern that against the projected Demand of Ministry of
DoNER for the year 2013-14 of Rs. 3614.91 crore only Rs. 2006.00 crore has been approved.
The Committee wonders as to also how the Ministry will make up for such a huge deficit
of Rs. 1608.91 crore and recommends the Ministry to take up the matter with the Planning
Commission and Ministry of Finance to enhance allocation at the RE Stage so that originally
envisaged course of actions are undertaken with enhanced allocation. This will, however,
depend on the expenditure pattern. (Para 2.3.4)
The Committee expresses its disappointment over the dismal achievement rate of
certain Plan schemes of the Ministry viz. capacity building and technical assistance NERLP,
NESRP and others where financial performance is below 50%. This situation calls for drastic
measure to improve the efficiency levels in order to justify proposed estimates which are,
more often than not, cut down because of lack of absorption capacity. The Committee would
like to highlight that the under utilization below 50% of allocated budget, would have
affected the achievement of physical targets and such situation would further negate the
fulfillment of projected demand for higher allocation in forthcoming financial year. The
Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the Ministry of DoNER must prevail upon
line departments/Ministries/Agencies to enhance their capacity to utilize allocated amount
scrupulously on the undertaken plans/projects/programs for their timely completion and
make a strong case with all supportive factors for higher allocation from the next financial
year onwards. (Para 2.3.6)
The Committee feels that the Ministry should have presented its case before the
Planning Commission more strongly to get its proposed T welfth Plan outlays appr oved. The
Committee recommends that the Ministry should improve its absorption capacities so that it can
demand more funds for various projects. The Committee finds that adverse effects of climate
change in NE Region can be seen from decreasing rain fall in the region and increasing melting
of glaciers. In view of the Committee, the NE Region has become highly vulnerable to the
consequences of climate change and the adaptation as well as mitigation projects are the need
of the hour. The Committee, therefore, recommends that Planning Commission should also
consider allocating funds for North-East Climate Change Adaptation Project. (Para 2.3.7)
The Committee notes the detailed reply of the Ministry on bottlenecks in
implementation of the projects, intensive monitoring thereof and scrupulous release of
funds for completion of projects. The Committee is not satisfied and convinced with the
detailed explanation and feels that all these steps appear to be a mere paper work in view
of the dismal financial achievements of the Ministry. The Committee also notes the
Ministry’s confession about its weakness in advocacy and coordination role, inadequate
technical support, inadequate over all staff support, inadequate space and absence of field
office. The Committee is of the strong view  that the purpose for which the Ministry was
set up, has not been fulfilled and it seems that the implementing ministries do not pay heed
to the requests or suggestions of the Ministry of DoNER. The Committee, therefore,
strongly, recommends that Government should consider the handicaps of the Ministry of
DoNER in a very serious manner and devise way out either by placing the Ministry of
50

51
DoNER under PMO directly or evolve some other mechanism so that the DoNER could get
implemented its decisions from the line Ministries/departments/agencies. (Para 2.3.11)
NORTH-EASTERN COUNCIL
The Committee notes the huge difference between the projected demand and actual
grant given to the North-Eastern Council. The allocation made is not even half of the
projected demand. The Committee fails to understand how the fund requirements would be
met for various projects. The Committee hopes that the NEC will find a way out to fill the
gap so that the projects do not suffer for want of funds. The Planning Commission and the
Ministry of Finance should also understand this problem and pave the way for providing
sufficient funds. (Para 2.4.4)
The Committee, while noting that the success of NEC efforts  depends heavily on the
cooperation from the State Governments, feels that the Council should evolve an incentive
structure for better performance so that performing States could be motivated to do better
and non-performing States may be made to feel that they may loose on account of non-
performance. (Para 2.4.8)
The Committee desires that the Council must also evolve mechanisms to complete
the projects on time despite very short working season in the North-East Region as one
cannot alter the geographical cycles. The Committee recommends that NEC may conduct a
comparative study on how projects are completed in other countries of similar climatic
conditions suffering from similar handicaps.  The Committee also notes unavailability of raw
material as well as limited capacity of contractors and executing agencies. The Committee
feels that the Government should come forward to address those deficiencies affecting
execution of the projects in NER by augmenting supply of raw material and assistance to
the executing agencies by providing soft loans to them. (Para 2.4.9)
CONSTRUCTION/IMPROVEMENT OF ROADS OF ECONOMIC IMPORTANCE

remains incomplete even after close to a decade. The Committee is aware that the State
Government of Manipur had earlier refused to implement the project and the same was
handed over to BRO for completion last year itself. The Committee, therefore, strongly
recommends that the construction of road be completed this year without any excuses. The
Committee further recommends that more projects should be identified to be taken up
under the scheme. (Para 2.5.3)
NON-PLAN LOANS TO NORTH-EASTERN HANDICRAFTS AND HANDLOOMS
DEVELOPMENT CORPORATION (NEHHDC)
The Committee understands the crucial role of NEHHDC in promotion and
development of handicrafts and handloom in the NER and therefore, feels that its revival
need to be done.  The Committee notes with concern that the earmarked allocation is not
sufficient as it falls short of Rs. 6.50 crore to implement Revival Plan of the Corporation,
which stands cleared by Cabinet Committee of Economic Affairs (CCEA). The Committee
urges upon the Finance Ministry to allocate the required amount so that NEHHDC may
make turn around in the year 2013-14 as per its projections. (Para 2.6.6)
LOAN TO NORTH-EASTERN REGIONAL AGRICULTURAL MARKETING CORPORATION
(NERAMAC)
Given its mandate of encouraging food processing units in NER and providing basic

52
infrastructure for marketing of agricultural and allied products, the allocation of Rs. 2.00
crore for BE 2013-14 to NERAMAC is too low for carrying out its activities. The Committee
notes that the allocation has remained the same for the years 2011-12 RE and 2012-13 BE.
The Committee, therefore, recommends that the Working Capital of the organization may
be increased as per its additional requirement of Rs.6.00 crore keeping in mind that the
corporation is a profit making organization with huge potential for growth. (Para 2.7.15)
The Committee notes that Fruit Juice Concentration Plant at Nalkata, Tripura, which
was able to absorb the entire production of pineapple grown in the area and was able to
provide better price to farmers, has outlived its life and requires renovation and
restructuring. The Committee is disappointed to note that despite its recommendation made
in 145th Report (Demands for Grants 2010-11) for early implementation of modernizing and
restructuring of the plant, the same has still not been done. Similarly, a Cashew Processing
Unit at Agartala in Tripura, which was able to absorb a major portion of the cashew nut
grown in Tripura, has also been closed due to strictures from Pollution Control Board. The
Committee has been informed that a proposal to relocate the plant is pending with Government
of Tripura. The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the requirement of
working capital may be provided immediately for increasing its activities manifold thereby
making huge impact on the farmers and producers of the region. (Para 2.7.16)
NORTH-EASTERN DEVELOPMENT FINANCE CORPORATION LIMITED (NEDFi)
North-Eastern Development Finance Corporation Limited (NEDFi) is an extremely
important Institution of the NER which provides term finance to industry, agro-horticulture
based industries and infrastructure along with services to the small entrepreneurs of the
region.The Committee has been informed that the Corporation is projecting internal
generation of around Rs. 300 crore, market borrowing of Rs. 90 crore and soft loan of
Rs. 60 crore from the Ministry of DoNER during the financial year 2013-14. The Committee
notes that though the Corporation has a target of 25-30 per cent growth on year-on-year
basis but it has scaled down its disbursement target from RS. 485.00 crore during the
financial year 2012-13 to Rs. 450 crore during the financial year 2013-14 due to resource
constraints. The Committee, therefore, recommends that adequate fund may be provided to
NEDFi at RE stage to carry out its activities as projected. (Para 2.8.14)
The Committee is given to understand that the corporation has fund requirement of
Rs. 5184 crore during the Twelfth Five Year Plan to meet the projected sanctions of
Rs. 6410.00 crore and disbursement of Rs. 4690.00 crore. The corporation has further
requested for interest-free loan to the tune of Rs. 1000.00 crore from the Government
during Twelfth Five Year Plan. Keeping in view the pivotal role of NEDFi, the Committee
reiterates its recommendation made in its 162nd Report on Demands for Grants (2012-13)
of the Ministry  that the Government should consider interest-free loan to the tune of
Rs. 1000.00 crore for ensuring NEDFi to meet its financial and physical targets during the
Twelfth Five Year Plan. (Para 2.8.15)
NON-LAPSABLE CENTRAL POOL OF RESOURCES (NLCPR)
The Committee is highly dismayed and extremely dissatisfied with the abysmal rate
of completion of projects under the scheme. The Committee was given similar excuses for
non-performance during the consideration of Demands for Grants (2012-13) which it noted
in its recommendation given in 162nd Report. The same set of excuses are again being
given this year like delay in tendering process, delay in transfer of funds to implementing
agencies, delay in utilization of funds and timely non-submission of correct and proper

53
documents by State Governments etc. The Committee feels that nothing has changed on
ground except for tall promises to rectify the situation. The Committee strongly
recommends that the various steps mooted by the Ministry should be implemented
immediately so that marked improvement gets visible in real terms by next financial year.
(Para 2.9.8)
The Committee notes the gap between grants released during 2009-2012 and
Utilisation Certificates submitted for the period by the States. While grants to the tune
Rs.2376.58 crore were released during the period, utilization certificates for only Rs.1838.78
Crore have been submitted by the States. This kind of non-submission of UCs creates
hurdles in the way of fresh allocation from the Pool for projects which, in turn, delays the
completion of projects causing time and cost overruns. The Committee urges upon the State
Governments concerned to submit Utilization Certificates on time so that funds could be
released on time and delays could be avoided. (Para 2.9.17)
The Committee notes that despite achieving budgetary targets and quarterly
expenditure targets, Grants from Central Pool of Resources for North-Eastern Region were
significantly reduced at the RE stage 2012-13 by the Finance Ministry. The Committee

be met. (Para 2.9.18)
BODOLAND TERRITORIAL COUNCIL (BTC)
The Committee notes that under the BTC Package of Rs. 500 crore, 42 projects at
approved cost of Rs. 476.27 crore have been sanctioned against which Rs. 453.34 crore have
been released by the Ministry. The Committee also notes that the Government of Assam
has submitted Utilization Certificates for only Rs. 398.07 crore. The Committee recommends
that the balance Utilization Certificates may be submitted at the earliest by the State
Government concerned. It also urges upon the Ministry to finish the remaining projects at
the earliest. The Committee also expresses concern over the under utilization of funds in
2012-13 even though it was reduced at RE stage. This needs to be looked into. (Para 2.10.6)
It has come to the notice of the Committee that the money from the Central fund
meant for BTC package has been lying with the State Government of Assam which  has not
been released. The Committee takes a serious view of this and feels that in federal set up
like India when the Central Government sanctions the fund the State Government has no
business to retain the fund without releasing for a longer period. It goes against the federal
principal. The Committee desires that the Central Government may review the entire
package and take up the matter with the State Government to ensure that such thing does
not recur in future. In case the State Government does not release the fund for the purpose
for which they are sanctioned, future release of the fund to the State Government may be
held up until the State Government takes necessary action. (Para 2.10.7)
ADVERTISING AND PUBLICITY
The Committee hopes that Plan allocation of Rs.7.00 crore would not be reduced at RE
stage as was done (allocation of Rs.7.00 crore reduced to Rs. 4.50 crore at RE Stage during
2012-13) so that Advertisement and Publicity is given due impetus this year. More efforts are
required to be taken in this regard to attract more investment in the region. (Para 2.11.6)

the set objective of the NERLP. The Committee therefore, recommends that concerted
efforts must be made in this direction. (Para 2.13.9)
SCHEME UNDER SPECIAL FUND FOR INFRASTRUCTURE UPGRADATION IN NORTH-

projects under the scheme on time. It also desires that these projects should be well

NORTH-EASTERN STATES ROADS INVESTMENT PROGRAMME
The Committee notes with displeasure that the allocation to the NESRI Programme
has been reduced owing to the inability of agencies to spend the allocations. It is also
disappointed to note that State Governments of Assam and Meghalaya have not been able
to claim mobilisation advance as their civil works contracts are yet to be approved. The

that the Ministry could successfully plead with Planning Commission for enhanced allocation
for the programme. When they cannot spend even the 25% of the allocation made at RE,

needs to be enhanced. (Para 2.15.4)

55
WORKING/MANDATE OF THE MINISTRY OF DoNER
The Committee fails to understand that a Ministry, which was carved out to focus
and expedite development in the North-east region, after more than a decade of its
existence has realized that it lacks sufficient power and necessary infrastructure to carry
out its mandate, and is completely dependent on various Line Ministries/Departments for
execution of projects. The Committee takes a serious view of the situation and feels that
a holistic view at the functioning and powers of the Ministry should be taken at this stage.
The Committee is not at all impressed with the functioning of the Ministry and gets an
impression that the line Ministries are not supporting or paying heed to the suggestions/
requests of the Ministry. The Committee intends to discuss this issue separately at a later
stage with all stakeholders and authorities. The Committee therefore recommends that the
Ministry should furnish a detailed note, based on the last 12-13 years of experience
indicating about the bottlenecks and shortcomings and the desired solutions. The Committee
also proposes to discuss the matter with the Cabinet Secretary and Secretaries of all the
line Ministries and the Chief Secretaries of the State Governments  so as to enable the
Ministry to effectively tackle the issues faced it. The Committee also intends to discuss with
the Planning Commission about the need for reviewing all the schemes being implemented
in the North-East to have a holistic view in the matter and also to find solutions to the
problems faced by the Ministry. (Para 3.1.2)
INFRASTRUCTURAL PROJECTS
The Committee is extremely concerned about abnormally long delays taking place in
execution of infrastructure projects in the Region. The Committee observes that the
Ministry comes up with similar alibis every time whenever they are asked about the delays.
The Committee, while acknowledging the fact that the region suffers from peculiar
problems, feels that a way out has to be found out, because neither the climate of the
region is going to change nor the region can be allowed to lag behind on the pretext of
adverse circumstances. The Committee recommends that the Ministry should look for
various technological interventions such as pre-fabricated structures, other innovative
methods and digitization of land records among others to speed up the process of project
execution. (Para 3.2.4)
POTENTIAL OF HYDRO-ELECTRIC (HE) PRODUCTION IN NE REGION
The Committee is at a loss to understand that despite such elaborate planning and
huge administrative mechanism, the realization of the potential remains abysmally low. The
Committee finds that even though Inter-Ministerial Groups (IMG), Task Force, Advisory
Groups and Special Monitoring Groups (SMG) were set up by the Government at one point
of time or other to sort out the problems afflicting the projects, yet perceptible outcome is
still a distant dream. (Para 3.3.7)
The Committee finds that while the identified potential in NE Region constitutes
about 40.1% of the total identified hydro power potential (145320 MW) in the country, but
only 1200 MW has so far been harnessed in NE region which is 2.06% of the identified
capacity and only 6 HE projects with aggregate capacity of 2852 MW (4.89%) are under
construction in NER. Even if the under construction projects in the region are completed on
time, the potential likely to be realized will only be close to 7%. This leaves a huge gap
between potential capacity and potential realized. In an energy deficit country like ours,
this is totally unacceptable. The Committee feels that the huge bureaucratic mechanism put
in place for the purpose and the policy guidelines adopted by themselves are not enough and

56
a spirited effort is required to make things happen on the ground. The Committee,
therefore, recommends that a very practical approach with quantifiable progress indicators
should be adopted for progress on ground. (Para 3.3.8)
The Committee feels that the Ministry of DoNER must play pro-active coordinating
role and act in tandem with Ministry of Water Resources, Power, Forest and Environment
and concerned State Governments in NER to harness Hydro power potential optimally.
(Para 3.3.9)
The Committee is extremely disappointed to note that Dimapur Power Project has
been abandoned after spending an amount of Rs. 90 crore. The Committee observes that
money spent on the project and subsequently abandoned, reflects lack of proper planning
and is a criminal wastage of fund. The Committee is of the considered opinion that the
project should have been more carefully planned and executed avoiding huge waste of
precious resources. (Para 3.3.11)
The Committee is astonished to find that on Lower Subansiri Project the estimated
completion cost has gone upto Rs. 11,000 crore and Government is losing Rs. 60 crore  for
every month of delay due to the concerns of the people over the Dam Safety. The
Committee recommends that the  Ministry after receiving the recommendations on Dam
Safety should attempt to win the confidence of the affected people by proper counseling so
that  the project takes off at the earliest. The Committee also hopes that once the project
gets started, the Ministry would ensure that the project is completed without further delay
and cost escalation. (Para 3.3.14)
ROAD CONNECTIVITY
As regards maintenance of roads, the Committee notes that neither the State
Governments have sufficient revenue nor the Central Government has any plan for the
purpose. Once the roads get deteriorated, the entire exercise has to be undertaken again.
The Committee, therefore, the Central Government may provide funds to the States for
maintenance of roads feels that until the economy of the NE States as a whole to improves.
(Para 3.4.9)
The Committee is not satisfied with the evasive replies of the Ministry for delay in
completion of the North-East component of the East-West corridor. The Committee is also
not satisfied with status of connectivity to all district headquarters of the NER as regards
connectivity by two-lane roads, as only 23 out of 88 district headquarters have been
connected by two-lane roads. The achievements are therefore extremely disappointing.
Despite its recommendations in several Reports for improving the pace of completion of
pending projects, the Committee has not witnessed any marked improvement on ground.
The Committee therefore, strongly recommends that concerted efforts on the part of the
concerned line Ministries are required for completing the undertaken projects within
stipulated time. (Para 3.4.10)
RAIL CONNECTIVITY
The Committee observes that several railway projects in NER suffer due to various
peculiarities viz., paucity of funds, limited working season, Militant activity and prevailing
security scenario in North-East Region, delay in land transfer to the project from State
Government and Forest clearance for Land. The Committee believes that such limiting
factors should not discourage the concerned line Ministry from extending its concerted
attention towards development of the region. The Committee, has, therefore, recommended

57
on several occasions that the best way to adhere is to properly plan and make strategy for
development keeping in view the limiting factors so that any development project is not
held up halfway. The Committee is of the view that the stumbling bloc such as limited
working season can be tackled by customized technological solutions while administrative
problems like forest clearances and land acquisition on time could be resolved by better
coordination and persuasion at highest level. (Para 3.6.5)
The Committee understands that militant activity and prevailing security scenario is,
of course, a larger problem which requires a national level brain-storming exercise and
towards that direction, the Union Ministry of Home Affairs and concerned State Government
should take appropriate steps together in a coordinated way. (Para 3.6.6)
The Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the Ministry of Railway should
leave no stone unturned for timely augmentation of  railway network i.e. 13 new lines, 4
gauge conversion and 1 doubling projects which have been taken up presently. Completion
of the projects as per schedule will go a long way in fulfilling the needs and aspirations of
local population and necessary funds may be provided for the purpose. The Ministry should
ensure that all the projects are completed as per the schedule and the targets fixed.  One
of the Railway Board Members should be made in-charge of the Railway Projects in the
North-East. That Member should regularly review the implementations of the Railway
projects on a quarterly basis. (Para 3.6.7)
AIR CONNECTIVITY
Good air connectivity to the North-East, like rest of the country, is a national
obligation and responsibility of the Government keeping in mind the difficult terrain and
strategic importance of the region. The Committee welcomes changes in the Route
Dispersal Guidelines of the Ministry of Civil Aviation that have made the public and private
airlines to fly in the North-East and thus facilitating not only people of the region to other
parts of the country but also people of other parts of the country travelling to NER.
(Para 3.7.5)
The Committee notes that night landing facilities are proposed to be extended to the
region besides the expansion of the runway, terminal buildings. The Committee believes that
steps being undertaken would improve air connectivity and related facilities. The Committee
urges upon the Ministry to complete Greenfield airport in Sikkim on schedule and commence
work for the construction of airports in Arunachal Pradesh and Nagaland. Keeping in view the
long pending public demand, the Committee also feels that Guwahati airport must be provided
with a second runway by converting the taxiway into a second runway so that it can serve as
an emergency runway. The Committee also recommends that the Ministry should explore the
possibility of making non-functional airstrips and airports operational for better air-connectivity
of the region in consultation with defence Ministry wherever possible. (Para 3.7.6)
INLAND WATER CONNECTIVITY
The Committee understands the importance of Inland Waterways as an alternative
to other modes of transport which are found lacking in many parts of the region. Inland
waterways has huge potential which can also be used to supplement the existing routes on
land. Waterways are the cheapest mode of transport anywhere in the world. In Western
European countries, about 40 per cent of the cargo movement is by waterways. The world’s
average is about 8 per cent, whereas in India it is less than 1 per cent. The Committee is
surprised to find that  in the National Water Policy, navigation comes almost towards the end
on the list of priority. The Committee, therefore, recommends that navigation in NER

58
should find priority as it is not only an economical mode of transport but also eco-friendly
and there is immense scope for improvement in the field of Inland Waterways in NER. The
Committee, therefore, strongly recommends that the Ministry of Shipping along with
Ministry of Water Resources should pursue all the projects vigorously in close coordination
with the Ministry of DoNER.  The Committee also recommends that fund constraints should
not come in the way of the implementation of projects. The Committee also recommends
that Inland Water Transport projects in Tripura, Meghalaya and Mizoram which are at
various stages of planning may be expedited and finalised. (Para 3.8.3)
The Committee notes with disappointment that Inland Waterway Terminal of Pandu
which is being developed as multi modal transit system is still hanging fire for want of
handing over of  land. The Committee directs that the matter should be taken up with the
NF Railway and resolved as soon as possible. The Committee further recommends that work
on proposed roll-on-roll-off terminals  at Dhubri and Hatsingimari be started immediately
without further delay. CPWD may take up the work on priority. (Para 3.8.4)
TOURISM
The Committee understands that there cannot be two opinions about the huge
potential for tourism that exists in the North-East but this potential has not been well
tapped so far. The Committee desires that the Ministry of Tourism should continue with its
concerted efforts by supporting projects for development of infrastructural facilities aiming
at promotion of tourism in the region. The Committee also recommends that projects of the
Master plan for Tourism be executed timely for promotion of tourism for the purpose.
(Para 3.9.6)
The Committee welcomes the idea of dividing the whole region into several tourist
circuits relating to religious and cultural tourism, wild life tourism, adventure tourism, eco-
tourism, tea tourism etc. which would cater to a large number of tourists, both national and
international. (Para 3.9.7)
The Committee understands that the continuation with special LTC scheme for
Government employees and creation of necessary human and physical capacities to absorb
such demand would further expand the number of tourists in NER. The Committee would
also like to suggest that Government may consider running of tourist trains on viable
tourist circuits in the NER, on the lines of tourist trains already running in other parts of
the country. (Para 3.9.8)
INDUSTRIAL SECTOR
The Committee takes into account the SWOT analysis of  the industrial situation in
NER and views that the Ministry of DoNER should make a detailed analysis of the same to
take up the issue of the industrial development in NER with the concerned line Ministries/
Departments. The Committee recommends that the following prospects of industrial
development in NER must be harnessed for ensuring balanced regional development:-
• The crude oil production and its refining as well as tea plantation and bamboo/
cane industries are the few resource-based industries in the region.
• Exploitation of the large hydro potential in the NER could be used for exporting
to the power deficit northern and western regions of the country.
• The Region’s comparative advantages in producing fruits, vegetables and other
horticulture products like spices can be tapped by setting up small-scale
processing units for the local market which would also boost rural employment.

59
• The North-East is an ideal destination for adventure, leisure and eco-tourism. The
mineral-rich North-Eastern States can also explore and promote geo-tourism.
• The education sector in the North-East has emerged as a major destination for
private firms. To explore the opportunities available, several private players are
now targeting the region to set up educational institutions which would serve the
cross-country market and cater to the needs of neighbouring countries.
• The North-Eastern Region is an ideal destination for Information Technology,
specifically for ITES sector. IT enabled service coupled with BPO business are
other areas which have enormous scope to flourish in the North–Eastern Region
because it has an advantage in its English speaking population and proficiency/
efficiency acknowledged by captains of IT industries outside the NER. This
should be explored to the full potential.
• Prospects for investors from outside the Region for setting up of industrial units
taking advantage of the incentives provided under NEIIPP–2007 by the Ministry
of Commerce and Industry.
• Since North-East is located at a crossroads between three major economies –
East Asia, South Asia and Southeast Asia, with the implementation of the ‘Look
East policy’ and opening up of trade routes, processing industries manufacturing
quality products, can be offered in international markets at competitive prices.
(Para 3.10.5)
The Committee believes that the spill-over benefits of industrial development for the
region would be the development of infrastructure such as roads, communications and
electricity supply to remote hilly areas, resulting in better quality of life. Natural gas based
industries are also feasible. The Committee also believes that NER could be an excellent
centre for horticulture, spices, and hub for educational and IT sector. (Para 3.10.6)
Since the region is expected to be declared as SEZ, there is every reason for the
Committee  to conclude that once the region is declared a SEZ by the Government of India,
there  would automatically come about a wide range of infrastructural development and a
rapid change in the industrial sector, opening scope for a rapid change in the socio-economic
scenario in the NE States. The Committee believes that industrial development can be made
in the NE States at par with the development in other regions of the country if all the steps
are taken in right ernest. The Committee recommends that the Government should make
concerted efforts in this direction. (Para 3.10.7)
The Committee is of the firm opinion that simultaneous growth of Micro, Small and
Medium Enterprises (MSMEs) along with big Business Enterprises can create an overall
growth story. Unfortunately the development pattern of the MSMEs of the Region is far from
encouraging. The Committee is of the firm view that the growth of MSMEs touches more
directly, the lives of common people and can raise their income levels much more drastically.
The Committee therefore, strongly recommends that Government must address the problems
being faced by the Micro, Small and Medium Enterprise (MSMEs). (Para 3.10.9)
EDUCATIONAL OPPORTUNITIES IN THE REGION
The Committee notes that in the absence of availability of adequate educational
opportunities in the region, students belonging to the region have to go to far flung areas
of the country. The Committee urges the Ministry of HRD to explore ways and means to
provide such opportunities in the NE Region establishing more institutes and provide
adequate number of faculty positions. (Para 3.11.1)

I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home
Affairs, having been authorized by the Committee to submit the report on its behalf, do hereby

Committees, the Chairman, Rajya Sabha, referred* the North-Eastern Council (Amendment)
Bill, 2013 as introduced in the Rajya Sabha on 11

of mutual interest to two or more States in the Region and to advise State Government(s) and
Central Government thereon. The Bill also seeks replacement of words “the Department of
Development of North-Eastern Region” with “Development of North-Eastern Region” in Section 6
of the Act.

REPORT
1.0 Background and objective of the Bill
1.1 The North–Eastern Council (Amendment) Bill, 2013 seeks to insert Section 3A after Section
3 and to amend Sections 4 and 6 of the North–Eastern Council Act, 1971 (herein after called
‘Principal Act’) which pertains to “Setting up and the composition of the North Eastern Council”,
‘Functions of the Council’ and “Nomination of certain officers to attend the meetings of the
Council” respectively. The proposed Section 3A to be inserted after Section 3 in the Act stipulates
that the term of office of two nominated members shall be three years which may be extended
for a further period not exceeding two years, while the allowances or remuneration payable to the
nominated members shall be such as may be determined by the Central Government. A new sub-
Section (1A) is proposed to be inserted in Section 4 of the Act to enable the Council to restore
the function of the Council to discuss any matter in which some or all of the States represented
in that Council, or the Union and one or more of the States represented in that Council, have a
common interest and advise the Central Government and the Government of each State concerned
as to the action to be taken on any such matter, and, in particular, may discuss and make
recommendations with regard to (i) any matter of common interest in the field of economic and
social planning; (ii) any matter concerning inter-State transport and communications; and (iii) any
matter relating to power or flood control projects of common interest. Further the proposed
amendment in Section 6 seeks to substitute the words ‘Development of North Eastern Region’ in
place of words ‘the Department of Development of North Eastern Region’.
1.2 The Statement of Object and Reason of the Bill spells out the details of the background and
objective as under:–
“The North-Eastern Council (NEC) was set up in 1972 by the North-Eastern Council
Act, 1971 for securing balanced and coordinated development and effecting coordination
among States of the north-eastern area viz. Arunachal Pradesh, Assam, Manipur, Meghalaya,
Mizoram, Nagaland and Tripura. The Governors and Chief Ministers of constituent States are
members of the Council. The North-Eastern Council (Amendment) Act, 2002, inter alia, added
Sikkim as the eighth member-State of the Council; envisaged functioning of the Council as
a regional planning body for the north-eastern area and provisioned for three members and
Chairman of the Council to be nominated by the President.
The nominated Union Minister, Governors and Chief Ministers of the constituent
States are members of the Council as long as they hold the office. Since establishment of
NEC, being a statutory body, is of permanent nature, therefore, tenure of nominated
members of the Council should be specified in the Act. Therefore, the Bill, inter alia, seeks
inclusion of (a) one member of the Planning Commission of India, being in charge of the
north-eastern region; (b) two non-official members nominated by the President for three
years period extendable for a further period not exceeding two years.
Second Administrative Reforms Commission, in its 7
th Report on ‘Capacity Building for
Conflict Resolution,’ inter alia, recommended for suitable amendment in the Act of 1971, to
restore the original ‘conflict resolution provision’ requiring the Council to discuss issues of
mutual interest of two or more States in the region and to advise the Central Government

th July,
2004 and recommendations of the Committee were examined in the Ministry and accordingly

(i) Appointment of Minister DoNER, as Chairman NEC
(ii) Equation of 3 nominated Members of NEC with Members of Planning Commission in
terms of rank, status (status of Minister of State of the Union Government), tenure
and emoluments and having them as full-time functionaries, headquartered at NEC
Secretariat, Shillong.
1.4 The Committee was further informed that the Cabinet approved the proposal of the Ministry
on 1
st December, 2004 with the modification that out of three nominated Members of the NEC,
one will be Member-in-charge of North East in Planning Commission. Through the proposed
amendment in Section 3, it is sought to specify that the Council shall, inter-alia , have (i) two non-
official members to be nominated by the President; (ii) one member of the Planning Commission
of India being in charge of the North-Eastern Region - ex officio. The Section 3A proposed to be
inserted after Section 3 in the principal Act stipulates that the term of office of two nominated
members shall be three years which may be extended for a further period not exceeding two years,
and the allowances or remuneration payable to the nominated members shall be such as may be

1.5 The Ministry of DoNER stated that an anomaly exists since tenure of Members of a statutory
body (NEC) was equated with tenure of a member of Planning Commission which is a non-statutory
and extra constitutional body set up by an executive order. According to the Ministry, this anomaly
has created a situation where, on expiry of the term of previous Government on the 18
th May, 2009,
all members of Planning Commission tendered their resignations, but non-official members of NEC
were not required to do so as per condition of their nomination. The current non-official members
(barring Member-NE, Planning Commission, who is an ex-officio non-official member) have now put
in around eight years. A statutory body must necessarily define tenure and conditions for their
removal (other than resignation and/or death), prior to their appointment as members, since life of
statutory body is independent of tenure of any Government formed by party/parties having majority
in Parliament. Committee on Revitalisation of NEC had recommended tenure of nominated members
as 3-5 years so as to have benefit of a cross section of experts drawn from different disciplines.

3
