3.4 MUNICIPAL CORPORATION OF CHANDIGARH
3.4.1 During the visit of the Sub-Committee, the Commissioner, Municipal Corporation of
Chandigarh also made a presentation before the Sub-Committee on 27
th July, 2012. According to
the Commissioner out of total area of 114 sq. km. of Chandigarh, the total area coming under the
jurisdiction of Municipal Corporation of Chandigarh is 79.34 sq. km. The Municipal area has
population of 9.44 lakh out of total population of 10.54 lakh. The entire area of Municipal
Corporation has been divided into 26 wards and each ward is represented by an elected councilor.
Besides, 9 members from amongst the persons, who are eminent/distinguished in public affairs, are
nominated by the Administrator, U.T. Chandigarh. The Member of Parliament from Chandigarh is
an ex-officio member. One third of total number of seats to be filled up by direct election is
reserved for women. Similarly, out of seats reserved for scheduled castes, one third seats are
reserved for women belonging to Scheduled Castes. Mayor is the Head of Elected Body assisted
by Sr. Deputy Mayor and Deputy Mayor. Obligatory and discretionary functions of the Corporation
are enshrined in Section 44 and 45 of the Municipal Act. Water supply and sewerage, storm water
drainage, street lighting, sanitation, community centres, roads and bridges, horticulture, fire
services, registration of births and deaths, primary health and primary education are major
functions entrusted to Municipal Corporation of Chandigarh.
3.4.2 The working of Municipal Corporation is based on the committee system under which
various Sub-Committees dealing with specified subjects, such as Finance and Contract, Water
supply and Sewerage disposal, Road, House Tax Assessment, Electricity, Environment and City
Beautification, Sanitation, Day Market and Apni Mandi, Fire and Emergency Services, Enforcement,
Arts Culture and Sports, Slum Colonies and Village Development exist. They are headed by a
Chairman whereas the Finance and Contract Committee is headed by Mayor. The financial power
of Finance and Contract Committee is upto R35 lakh. The tenure of these Committees is one year.
Different Committees have been delegated financial and other powers to carry on the functions
relating to Municipal Corporation. The matter involving financial implication beyond
R35 lakh and policy decisions are placed before the General body (House) meeting of the
Corporation.
3.4.3 The UT Administration was asked about steps required to further strengthen the working
of Municipal Corporation of Chandigarh. The UT Administration submitted that since its inception
various functions/departments have been transferred to Municipal Corporation in a phased manner,
as a result of which the responsibilities of the Corporation have been increased considerably.
Therefore, it requires strengthening of the Corporation by taking following steps:–
● Strengthening of manpower
● Strengthening of infrastructure/machinery
● Strengthening of MCC using Information Technology
● Increase in Annual Budget.

31
3.4.4 The UT Administration was asked whether allocated budgetary provisions are sufficient for
carrying out the development projects. In its response, it was stated that the allocated budgetary
provision is insufficient for carrying out the development projects. About 10.83% of the budget
(Plan and Non Plan) of Chandigarh is allocated to MCC. 17.5% of the Tax Revenue of
Administration is paid on Grant-in-Aid to the MCC as per the recommendations of 3rd Delhi
Finance Commission.
3.4.5 On the question of criteria for devolution of funds to the Local Bodies keeping in view the
increasing functions and jurisdiction of Municipal Corporation, Chandigarh, the UT Administration
stated that no criteria for devolution of funds to the Local Bodies has been conveyed to the
Chandigarh Administration by the Government of India. However, Chandigarh Administration is
providing financial aid to Municipal Corporation, Chandigarh on account of developmental works
from the Plan budget in addition to Government of India Grant being paid as per the
recommendations of 3rd Delhi Finance Commission.
3.4.6 The UT Administration was asked whether it is being contemplated to increase the revenue
of Municipal Corporation as the Corporation has more responsibility with limited authority and
financial resources. The UT Administration in its response has admitted that it is being
contemplated to increase the revenue of MC, U.T. Chandigarh. Recently, Municipal Corporation has
imposed tax on residential property @ R1/- per square yard. This will increase the revenue of the
Municipal Corporation, U.T., Chandigarh and the revision of proposed rates of Tax is under
examination of the Municipal Corporation, Chandigarh.
3.4.7 According to the UT Administration, the fourth Delhi Finance Commission has been
constituted to find out the shortcomings in the budgetary provisions. The detailed report has been
given to the Delhi Finance Commission to consider and suggest ways and means to increase the
revenue share of the Municipal Corporation, Chandigarh. The measures so suggested by the Fourth
Delhi Finance Commission shall be further examined for adoption.
3.4.8 The Committee recommends that increasing financial power of Finance and Contract
Committee of Chandigarh Municipal Corporation which is headed by Mayor upto one crore
rupees should be considered as keeping in view the municipal area of Chandigarh, 35 lakh
is meager amount.
3.4.9 The Committee also recommends that strengthening of manpower and infrastructure
of MCC is the handicap in its efficient discharge of mandate. Strengthening of MCC in
terms of using Information Technology is also required. The Committee therefore
recommends that the UT Administration should take all corrective actions proactively to
remove hurdles in the way of MCC. Besides, there should be maximum use of information
technology in the offices of Municipal body so that residents could get their work done
hassle free.
3.4.10 After going through details of budgetary provisions and expenditure during the last
five years of Municipal Corporation of Chandigarh, the Committee disapprovingly notes that
the Municipal Corporation has not been able to spend the allocated amount in any financial
year. The Committee views that the demand of the UT Administration for more money to
MCC as the allocated budgetary provision is insufficient for carrying out the development
projects is misplaced. The Committee recommends that the MCC should strive to increase
its fund absorption capacity for carrying out the development projects in the municipal area
of the UT with alacrity.
3.5 ISSUES PERTAINING TO INDUSTRIES OF CHANDIGARH
3.5.1 The Committee received representations from Industries Association of Chandigarh on the

32
issues pertaining to the industries in Chandigarh which was forwarded to the Ministry for replies/
comments. The issues are being discussed below:–
Proper implementation of the Act MSMED Act, 2006
3.5.2 The MSMED Act, 2006 should be implemented in the UT properly and more activities
should be allowed in the industrial area by proper implementation of. By virtue of this Act,
Parliament in its wisdom had decided to redefine Small Scale Industry by renaming it as Enterprise
to include manufacturing and services.
Response of the Ministry
3.5.3 Allowing of more activities has no relevance with MSMED Act as it is governed by the
local Building Bye-laws/Urban Planning Rules and Master Plan because of change of land use and
is subject-matter under State list of the Seventh Schedule of the Constitution. Activities of IT and
ITES in Industrial Area were earlier not being permitted because the city has an SEZ in the name
of Rajiv Gandhi Chandigarh Technology Park and allowing of these activities in the old Industrial
Estates could impact the development of the IT Park. Now, this issue has been discussed at the
highest level of the Administration and it has been felt that no notification is needed as IT (software
and hardware development) being of the manufacturing nature and is permissible in the Industrial
area. As regards the notices already issued for misuse because of such activities being carried out
in the Industrial Area in place of other manufacturing activities, it was decided that such notices
issued shall be dropped by the Estate Office and thus, the issue has been resolved.
3.5.4 The Committee understands that in MSMED Act, the word ‘industry’ has expressly
been replaced by ‘enterprises’, due to which services along with manufacturing are allowed.
The UT administration should implement the said Act in letter and spirit. Early action may
be taken to drop the notices.
Industrial Policy
3.5.5 There was also an issue of Industrial Policy which is to be implemented soon.
Response of the Ministry
3.5.6 The city of Chandigarh has a special Heritage Status and in order to maintain its pristine
glory, a major policy-decision was taken in the year 2006 vide notification on 04.07.2006, which
postulates the broad parameters of the Industrial policy. Its implementation is regulated by Urban
Planning laws, Master plan (Land-use plans) and enforced through Estate Office. The relevant
portion of the Notification is reproduced below:–
“the plots/sheds shall hence-forth be allotted to Industrial houses for promotion of
Information Technology, precision-equipment manufacturing, Electronic Industry-related
projects without any discharge of effluent nor any source of emission by keeping the reserve
price close to the market rates or by way of auction etc. for which detailed modalities
would be worked-out separately” .
3.5.7 According to the UT Administration, that draft-policy is under process and is likely to be
notified shortly.
3.5.8 The Committee notes that the draft Industrial Policy is under process and is likely to
be notified. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Home Affairs (MHA) should
impress upon the UT administration for redrafting new industrial policy of UT in consonance
with the MSMED Act, 2006 which the Centre had formulated for the overall industrial growth

33
and accommodate the grievances of local industrialists. The UT Administration should also
invite objections/suggestions from stakeholders of the industry before finalising the policy.
3.5.9 The Committee understands that promotion of pollution free, energy-efficient, hi-
tech, low-volume and high value-added industries is needed for the UT. However, interests
of other less polluting manufacturing industries in small and micro segment also needed to
be protected. The Committee desires that the Ministry should look into the matter.
Misuse charges at R500/- per sq.ft. per month

Buildings from time to time for the alleged violations which have been usually carried out by the
tenants and this leads to disputes between the landlords and tenants pending before the Courts. The
rates of penalties for alleged violations are on very higher side which is R500 per square per
month. This has led to shifting of business to satellite towns.
Response of the Ministry
3.5.11 The rates were revised by way of a notification way back in 2007 and thus carry sanctity
of law as on date to serve as a deterrent so that misuse or unauthorized conversion of activities
is discouraged by making it unviable with the penal charges. However, the Ministry has informed
that there is a move to review these charges for downward revision.
3.5.12 The Committee understands that the revised rates carry the sanctity of law as on
date to serve as a deterrent to unauthorized conversion of activities. The Committee
recommends that the UT Administration should undertake downward revision of the charges
on priority basis and notify the same at the earliest.
Conversion of Industrial Plots from lease holds tenure to free hold tenure
3.5.13 There was a demand of conversion of Industrial Plots from lease holds tenure to free hold
tenure as it is prevalent thorough out the country.
Response of the Ministry
3.5.14 The matter has been considered in detail and it has been observed by the competent
authority that since the properties have been allotted on lease basis for 99 years and there is no
reason for conversion of properties other than residential allotted on lease hold basis to be
converted into free hold, there is no move to allow the conversion of Industrial plots from lease

hold land tenure to free hold tenure may be considered appropriately.
Simplification of Procedures

and returns of the dealers/industry would be made online .

34

Administration should complete its ongoing computerization work at the earliest to facilitate

the Departments of UT particularly in service based Departments so that people could get

Single Window System

Air connectivity

flights timings for the existing flights also need to be rescheduled so that a person is able to reach

Response of the Ministry
3.5.23 The issues raised in the representation would be taken up with the concerned Ministry.
3.5.24 The Committee agrees that the city of Chandigarh should be connected with all
major cities of the country. The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Home Affairs
should take up the issue with the Ministry of Civil Aviation for running more flights and

goods/services/people.
Railways

the quality of service in Shatabdi Express has deteriorated adversely. Better quality and service are

3.5.26 The issues raised in the representation would be taken up with the concerned Ministry.

goods/services/people with the Ministry of Railways. Other issues may also be taken up.

3.5.33 In the industrial plots, there is a need to cover the open spaces with corrugated sheets

36
3.5.34 The Committee understands the need of covering the open spaces with corrugated
sheets to prevent losses due to unseen reasons. The Committee recommends that The

allowed to operate from Industrial Area.

Federation and Tenement Colonies regarding the problems being faced by residents of CHB and

Ownership rights to the residents of the tenement colonies

last decades bought their houses on power of attorney.
Response of the Ministry
3.6.3 The proposal has already been examined in detail and it has been recommended for
consideration at the senior level for transfer of ownership rights on lease-hold basis to those who
are having the documents like GPA and other evidence of transaction and transfer of possession
as per CHB/Estate Office policy and if approved, the move will benefit 3500 persons of transferees
out of total 11670 persons subject to their possessing the requisite documents.
3.6.4 The Committee desires that the UT Administration should sympathetically consider
the plight of residents of the tenement colonies who over the last decades bought their
houses on power of attorney and give them ownership rights. The Ministry of Home Affairs

Additions made on land by one-room owners
3.6.5 The need-based small additions made on small unused patches of land by one-room owners
to accommodate their growing families should be compounded.
Response of the Ministry
3.6.6 The UT Administration informed that this basically is a request to regularize the
encroachments on Government land which cannot be regularized without proper allotment and
examination of the implications. It is also informed that at present, there is no such regularization
possible.
3.6.7 The Committee understands that small additions made on small unused patches of
land by one-room owners to accommodate their growing families is not sanctioned by law.

and take an early decision.
Delinking of the inspection for building violations with/from the process of transfer of ownership
3.6.8 There was a demand of delinking of the inspection for building violations with/from the
process of transfer of ownership by Chandigarh Housing Board Residents Federation.
Response of the Ministry
3.6.9 In response, the UT Administration has stated that there have been a lot of violations of
the existing bye laws of the Capital of Punjab (Development and Regulation) Act, 1952. According

39
to the UT Administration, a survey was conducted in 2000 wherein it was found that 75-80% of
building violations exist in the Dwelling Units of Chandigarh Housing Board. It has mentioned that
as per procedure, the Dwelling Units are being converted from lease hold to free hold basis under
the Chandigarh Conversion of Residential Lease-hold Land Tenure into Free hold Land Tenure
Rules, 1996. The conversion charges are fixed by the Estate Officer, UT, Chandigarh and collected
on behalf of the Estate Office. According to the UT Administration, the CHB only issues the
conversion letter to the applicants for executing Conveyance Deed with the Registrar, UT,
Chandigarh. When the applicant applies for transfer of ownership on the basis of GPA and Sale
Deed, the CHB as per procedure takes the building violation/misuse report. In case, there is building
violation, the case is not approved and the applicant is informed that his request cannot be
considered until and unless the violations are removed. The UT Administration has mentioned that
now the proposal is being submitted to the Board for consideration and approval for allowing
transfer on the basis of affidavit of the applicant stating therein that there is no building violation/
misuse in the dwelling unit.
3.6.10 The UT Administration has further mentioned that the CHB is transferring the dwelling unit
on the basis of GPA/Sub-GPA, where the transaction has taken place after a lock-in period of
5 years from the date of physical possession as per provisions of the approved GPA transfer policy
under Regulation-16 of Chandigarh Housing Board (Allotment, Management and Sale of Tenements)
Regulations, 1979. In such cases, a no-violation report is presently being taken. It has also
informed that the proposal is being submitted to the Board for consideration and approval on the
basis of affidavit submitted by the applicant.
3.6.11 On the issue of delinking of the inspection for building violations from the process

“16 Transfer of Registration/property: - Notwithstanding anything contained in these

Participatory Democracy

42
setting up of super specialty Hospitals in private sectors on the pattern of adjoining town of Mohali

3.7.14 UT Chandigarh has the shortage of power to the tune of 50-60 MW presently but this

1. The setting up of Thermal and Hydro Power Plants are not viable in UT Chandigarh

2. Further, gas based power plant in UT Chandigarh is not feasible in view of the
following facts:–
(a) Setting up of gas based power plant requires land which is very difficult to be

mention here that land for already proposed new 220 kV Grid Station which is

and skilled manpower, which is not available to CED at present. It is worth to
mention here that CED is already struggling with the problem of manpower
shortage in maintaining power distribution function alone.

43
(c) It may be very difficult in getting environmental and other necessary clearances

(d) For setting up of SPV Solar Plant in UT Chandigarh, M/S CREST has been

Shortage of Drinking Water
3.7.28 The non-cooperative attitude of adjoining States of Punjab and Haryana in not allowing
water from Bhakra Canal for augmentation of water supply scheme of the city from Kaujoliwater
works has further exaggerated the problem. River water is a Natural National Resource and the

greater say in settling such interstate disputes.

45
Response of the Ministry
3.7.29 The quantity of drinking water available to the City residents is 87 MGD which is made
available through two main sources viz. (i) from 210 deep tube wells (underground water)=20
MGD; (ii) from Bhakra Canal located 28 km. from the city (Surface water brought to city through
4 pipelines)=58 MGD; (iii) Share of Panchkula and Chandimandir of Bhakra water presently being
used by Chandigarh city=9 MGD. As per real time data available with the Municipal Corporation
through its billing, it is observed that city residents are being supplied 252 ltrs. per capita per day
(lpcd) which is much above the national norm of 135 lpcd. As such, there is no shortage of
drinking water supply in the city. To maintain adequate pressure in all the areas, 70 water boosting
stations scattered all over the city have been constructed and are in operation. These boosting
stations maintain adequate pressure in otherwise low pressure areas. During the current summer
season, the consumer satisfaction regarding supply of drinking water was found to be much higher
than the previous years due to continuous monitoring/management/ checking of leakages by the
Public Health wing of MCC. During peak summer season, the demand of drinking water rises and
estimated shortfall is 29 MGD. In order to meet this peak demand, a project to bring 40 MGD
additional water from Bhakra Main line at Kajauli got approved under JNNURM but it could not
be executed due to non availability of consent of the States of Punjab and Haryana due to their
interstate issues. However, GMADA is laying a bigger dia pipeline of capacity 80 MGD for bringing
water from Bhakra Main Line at Kajauli to Mohali and satellite towns. Efforts are being made to
persue the States of Punjab and Haryana for releasing 40 MGD for Chandigarh which can be
brought to the city through this bigger dia pipeline. Chandigarh has implemented an ambitious
project under JNNURM to supply tertiary water to all the green belts, gardens and houses having
area more than 1 kanal. The tertiary water plant along with rising main and network of pipes
supplying tertiary water to all areas of the city has since been commissioned and is in operation.
All big institutions, golf club, golf course, green belts, gardens and neighbourhood parks have been
covered with tertiary treated water. The tariff rates for supply of tertiary treated water have been
kept low by the MCC in order to promote its usages in big way so as to conserve fresh water
which otherwise is being used for irrigation by big households. Regarding recharging of water
through rain water harvesting, work has been entrusted to Centre for Science and Environment,
New Delhi for preparing a pilot project for one sector of the city. After studying the results of
this project, it can be replicated to other parts of the city.
3.7.30 The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Home Affairs should take up this
matter at the highest level for getting water from Bhakra Canal for augmentation of
Kajouli water works. The UT administration should also promote water conservation through
rain water harvesting and ground water recharge etc. in the UT to tackle water woes and
ensure long-term sustainability of water sources for the city. A comprehensive water use
audit should also be done in all the houses, residential and commercial buildings. The
Citizens of the UT may be encouraged to conserve water through rainwater harvesting,
recycling and reusing water and reducing water wastage. Pilot project for rain water
harvesting may be implemented at the earliest.
Poor Solid Waste Management system

regulate the disposal of solid waste.
Response of the Ministry
3.7.32 The Municipal Corporation, Chandigarh has already framed Chandigarh Municipal
Corporation (Sanitation and Public Health) Bye Laws, 1999. The Municipal Corporation Chandigarh

46
manages Solid Waste in 56 Sectors, 41 urban slums/colonies and 9 villages apart from erstwhile
N.A.C. Manimajra. Approximately 350 – 400 tonnes of Municipal Solid waste is generated per day
by the city i.e. Sectors/urban slums/colonies/villages. The residential garbage is being collected door
to door which after segregation is put in the garbage bins. The safaikaramcharies collect the
garbage and transfer it in the garbage bins. The Garbage is transported by deploying fast moving
dumper placers for 4.5 Cubic M Capacity containers. Tractor Trolleys, Refuse Collector
Compactors etc. are also pressed into service for transportation of garbage. To maintain the city
sanitation, 25 new Dumper placers and 200 new garbage bins have been procured in order to
provide aesthetic look of ‘City Beautiful’ and quick mobility of the Solid Waste from the city limits
for dumping. 200 Garbage bins have also been got repaired. The seasonal wastes i.e. dry leaves
etc. generated during the year are removed from the various Sectors/urban slums/colonies/villages
by deploying additional tractor trolleys with manpower so as to make the city free from the dry
leaves etc. The final disposal of the Municipal Solid Waste is done by processing the same through
Garbage Processing Plant which has been established on BOOT basis wherein the city garbage is
processed to form Refuse Derived Fuel (RDF). The Chandigarh Administration and the Municipal
Corporation took the initiative for commissioning of Garbage Processing Plant in the West of
Sector 25, Dadu Majra Chandigarh on BOOT (Built Own Operate and Transfer) basis to M/s Jai
Prakash Associates Ltd. wherein the plant management has set up the required machinery. All the
expenditure for setting up the Plant has been borne by the Project Developer. In view of the new
technology the same is being monitored for making the venture successful to produce Refuse
Derived Fuel to achieve the ultimate goal as to disposal and Processing of Municipal Solid Waste
as per the Municipal Solid Waste (Management and Handling) Rules, 2000. The Garbage Processing
Plant is processing approximately 250-300 MT Municipal Solid Waste everyday. The Management
of Garbage Processing Plant has also installed Hot Air Generator to process the wet garbage. The
monitoring of Garbage Processing Plant and Dumping Site is being looked after by the Engineering
Wing of Municipal Corporation, Chandigarh.
3.7.33 Reclamation of existing Dumping Site: The dumping site is spread in an area of 45 acres.
Out of this, 25 acres have been reclaimed scientifically as per the Municipal Solid Waste
(Management and handling) Rules, 2000. The landfill has been made in an approximate area of 8
acres and closing, covering and capping has been completed for approximately 17 acres with the
funds contributed by Central Pollution Control Board New Delhi, Chandigarh Administration and
Municipal Corporation, Chandigarh. The remaining 20 acres area is being used for dumping the
rejects/inerts from the Garbage Processing Plant and the waste coming from Sabzi Mandies,
ApniMandies, Big hotels, villages including villages under the Chandigarh Administration. The
dumped waste is leveled by using chain dozers. Effective Micro organism and micro nutrient
solution is sprayed three times a day over the waste to sanitize and make the garbage odourless.
A layer of malba/soil is spread over the waste using JCB, Tippers and chain dozers. The Dumping
Ground is properly fenced and buffer zone has been created around the Dumping Ground.
3.7.34 Installation of Bio Gas Plants: The Municipal Corporation (Engineering Wing) Chandigarh is
considering to install two Bio Gas Plants to Process the Hotel Waste, Vegetable Waste, mixed Waste
i.e. Horticulture and mixed garbage etc.
3.7.35 W ith the strenuous efforts made by the Municipal Corporation, Chandigarh to keep the City
Clean, Chandigarh has been adjudged as First by Ministry of Urban Development, on the basis of
National Rating Survey Data on City Sanitation in the recent past.

the UT. The Committee understands that solid waste management will be a key challenge
for any rapidly growing city. The Committee understands that for a viable solid waste
service delivery, the UT Administration should explore cost-effective environmental friendly

options to conserve natural resources and preserve landfill space, seek continuous

Drying up of Sukhnalake
3.7.51 There is likelihood of drying up of the Sukhnalake.

49
Response of the Ministry
3.7.52 Sukhna Lake is an artificial rain fed lake created in 1958. It has been observed that
whenever there is deficient rainfall in two successive years, the Sukhna Lake gets dried up for
about 1-2 months in the peak of summer months. This has happened 2-3 times in last 10 years.
However, the lake receives water as soon as monsoon arrives. There is no likelihood of Sukhna
Lake drying up permanently.
3.7.53 The Committee understands that Chandigarh is known for its famous Sukhna Lake
which is the most-visited tourist place in the area. With the lake not getting enough water
due to poor monsoon, it turns into a dried bed. As it is completely a rainfed lake
occasionally drying up due to periodic occurrence of deficit rainfall. The Committee
recommends that a think tank should be involved in this matter. Besides, There should be
a permanent body for its conservation and monitoring and its members should be drawn
from experts from the field of hydrology, soil, ecology, wildlife etc. A long term plan may
be prepared for conserving the lake.
3.8 ISSUES CONCERNING ELECTRICITY DEPARTMENT
Privatization
3.8.1 It was demanded that the contemplated move to privatize/corporatize the Electricity
Department should be stopped as the move is against the interest of general public as well as
employees. Ever since the reorganization of the States and creation of Chandigarh in November,
1966, this Department has been functioning quite efficiently and is profit making, except last 2
years due to inefficiency of the controlling officers, even though the rates are less than that are
being charged in Punjab and Haryana. Electricity, being one of the most basic necessities for
growth of economy, had been kept in the hands of the government, either as a department or as
a state controlled public sector undertaking.
Response of the Ministry
3.8.2 Chandigarh Electricity Department (CED) is implementing the provisions of Electricity
Act, 2003 passed by the Parliament and the National Electricity Policy, 2005. In the Electricity
Act, 2003, reorganization of the board is provided under part-13 of the Act. Further, following
provisions have been provided under Para 5.4.3 of the Electricity Policy, 2005:
“5.4.3: For achieving efficiency gains proper restructuring of distribution utilities is
essential. Adequate transition financing support would also be necessary for these utilities.
Such support should be arranged linked to attainment of predetermined efficiency
improvements and reduction in cash losses and putting in place appropriate governance
structure for insulating the service providers from extraneous interference while at the same
time ensuring transparency and accountability. For ensuring financial viability and
sustainability, State Governments would need to restructure the liabilities of the State
Electricity Boards to ensure that the successor companies are not burdened with past
liabilities. The Central Government would also assist the States, which develop a clear road
map for turn around, in arranging transition financing from various sources which shall be
linked to predetermined improvements and efficiency gains aimed at attaining financial
viability and also putting in place appropriate governance structures.”
3.8.3 Therefore, Chandigarh Electricity Department is only implementing the provisions of the
Electricity Act, 2003/National Electricity Policy.

50
3.8.4 The Committee is of the view that while implementing the provisions of Electricity
Act, 2003 efforts should be made to protect the interests of the public and employees.
Inadequacy of Staff
3.8.5 The U.T. Powermen Union drew attention to the inadequacy of staff and equipments. The posts
that fell vacant have not been filled up and sanctioned posts to meet the increasing workload have
remained unfilled and even S.I.U. report has also not been implemented as the Central Government has
placed an embargo without any reasonable ‘justification’. These result in delay in extending services to
the public, giving rise to avoidable complaints. Administration was requested to consider these
shortcomings objectively to equip the Department to enable it to meet the demands of service of the
consumers as well as implementation of JERC decision i.e. standard of performance.
Response of the Ministry
3.8.6 The Electricity Department is regulated by the Joint Electricity Regulatory Commission.
Though CED requested to allow filling up of vacant posts but the JERC is not allowing filling up
of the vacant posts. Last year also, JERC has allowed filling up of 209  vacant posts for the
financial year 2012-13. A review petition was filed on this account which was also rejected by
the JERC. Again, the Department requested to allow to fill up 129 posts for the financial year
2013-14 but the JERC did not approve the same. Following orders have been passed in the tariff
order dated 15.04.2013 by the JERC for the financial year 2013-14 :
“---it is stated that considering an All India average number of employee per thousand
consumers is 0.405 ( i.e.  one employee per 2500 number of consumers). It can be
construed that the Electricity Department of Chandigarh is not understaffed. Hence, the
Commission does not consider and does not approve the manpower recruitment of nearly
129 employees for FY 2013-14. However, a few IT, Commercial and Accounts Officers
may be considered for recruitments in equal number as employees to fill the vacancies
created due to superannuation of employees and who will continue to provide the service
in line with the Standard of Performance of Distribution Code Regulations.”
3.8.7 The Committee desires that the issue of inadequacy of staff and equipments in the
Electricity Department may be resolved at the earliest.
3.9 ISSUES CONCERNING CHANDIGARH TRANSPORT UNDERTAKING
Vacant Posts

3.9.2 UT Administration has already conducted written test for the post of Drivers and declared

the recruitment of Conductors at the earliest. Besides, recruitment notification for vacant

51
posts of workshop staff, management staff, and Class-IV staff should also be advertised

this regard. (Para 3.5.43)
The UT of Chandigarh Administration should involve citizens groups, public
representatives in all major decision making processes so that grievances and problems of
people could come to the fore and hence their redressal. (Para 3.5.46)
The Committee desires that the issue may be solved by the UT Administration at the
earliest by holding discussion with them. (Para 3.5.49)
The Committee notes the reply and feels that there should be some mechanism for
disposing of the pending Sale Tax Assessment Cases prior to implementations of V AT. The
Ministry of Home Affairs may take up this issue with the Finance Ministry. (Para 3.5.52)
The Committee desires that the UT Administration should sympathetically consider
the plight of residents of the tenement colonies who over the last decades bought their
houses on power of attorney and give them ownership rights. The Ministry of Home Affairs
should consider this and take an early decision. (Para 3.6.4)
The Committee understands that small additions made on small unused patches of
land by one-room owners to accommodate their growing families is not sanctioned by law.
However, the Committee recommends that the UT Administration should look into this issue
and take an early decision. (Para 3.6.7)
On the issue of delinking of the inspection for building violations from the process
of transfer of ownership by Chandigarh Housing Board Residents Federation, the Committee
is of the opinion that the issue has merit and the UT Administration should reconsider its
decision in this regard. (Para 3.6.11)
The Committee notes that the UT Administration is considering a onetime relaxation
for transfer on GPA basis to the transactions within the lock-in period of five years. The
Committee desires that early decision may be taken in the matter. (Para 3.6.17)

61
The Committee notes the submission of the administration that the rates are under
consideration of UT Administration. The Committee recommends that the UT administration
should increase/fix rate by taking into account the problems of the people. The Committee
is of the view that market rate of land should not be applied for permitted extra coverage
in Residential Houses . (Para 3.6.20)
The Committee observes that the recent years have witnessed a keen interest of
people in participation in decision making process of Governments. The Committee is of the
view that the UT Government should involve NGOs, Civil Society Groups, citizen groups in
shaping decisions and deliberating over policies that affect their lives and also put draft
policies for public scrutiny. Involving citizens in the decision making process will lead to
transparency and good governance. (Para 3.7.3)
The Committee is of the view that UT Administration should endeavour to preserve
the original character of the city. The Committee recommends that proposed Master Plan
of Chandigarh should incorporate this concern of the citizenry. (Para 3.7.6)
The Committee recommends that Chandigarh Administration should expedite the
completion of the study for improvement of traffic and transportation and consider the
same while finalizing the proposed Master Plan. (Para 3.7.9)
The Committee recommends that the UT Government should take early decision for
setting up of a 500 bedded General Hospital in the southern sector as proposed by the
Health Department without any delay. (Para 3.7.12)
The Committee understands that UT of Chandigarh has no power generation of its
own and has to buy power from outside throughout the year. Therefore, the Committee
recommends that land required for proposed new 220 kV Grid Station may be allocated by
the Administration on priority basis without any procedural delay. (Para 3.7.15)
The Committee recommends that problems of civic amenities like roads, drainage
systems, street lights, parks, markets, bus shelters, primary health centres post office,
community centers etc. in southern sectors of the city should be addressed by the
administration to the extent possible now as these basic amenities cannot wait for
finalization of the Master Plan. However, all these amenities should be included in the
Master Plan. (Para 3.7.18)
The Committee desires that the UT Administration should make all out efforts to
make the city crime free. The Chandigarh Police should improve patrolling and intelligence
gathering mechanism. (Para 3.7.21)
The Committee understands that Right to Service Act if implemented effectively and
efficiently it would fast track grievance redressal and check corruption. The Committee
recommends that the UT Administration should finalise soon services to be covered under
the Right to Service Act, 2013 and the Act be notified at the earliest. (Para 3.7.24)
The Committee desires that the UT Government should simplify the departmental
procedures particularly in public service departments by putting effective and user friendly
systems in place. This will help the citizens get their work done without any hassle and will
also help the Government in its functioning. The UT Administration should remove the
procedural complexity which causes delay. (Para 3.7.27)
The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Home Affairs should take up this
matter at the highest level for getting water from Bhakra Canal for augmentation of
Kajouli water works. The UT Administration should also promote water conservation

62
through rain water harvesting and ground water recharge etc. in the UT to tackle water
woesand ensure long-term sustainability of water sources for the city.A comprehensive water
use audit should also be done in all the houses, residential and commercial buildings. The
Citizens of the UT may be encouraged to conserve water through rainwater harvesting,
recycling and reusing water and reducing water wastage. Pilot project for rain water
harvesting may be implemented at the earliest. (Para 3.7.30)
The Committee appreciates the solid waste management mechanism functional in the
UT. The Committee understands that solid waste management will be a key challenge for
any rapidly growing city. The Committee understands that for a viable solid waste service
delivery, the UT Administration should explore cost-effective environmental friendly options
to conserve natural resources and preserve landfill space, seek continuous improvements to
reduce the cost of operations, evolve strategic partnerships with public, private and civil
society groups in the UT. (Para 3.7.36)
The Committee understands that the mandate of Chandigarh Housing Board (CHB)
is to build affordable, reasonably priced dwelling units for different socio-economic
categories of the city’s residents and it has also been entrusted the work of implementing
the administration’s schemes for rehabilitating the residents of unauthorized settlements.
The Committee hopes that the CHB would work in this direction in future. (Para 3.7.41)
The Committee recommends that the issue of allotment of flats to the employees
may be resolved soon. If need be, they may be accommodated in any proposed scheme on
priority basis. (Para 3.7.44)
The Committee understands that the focus of Chandigarh Housing Board should be
making Chandigarh a slum free city. Considering the gravity of the problem of housing for
poor in Chandigarh, it should take responsibility for providing affordable housing to the
urban poor. The Committee hopes that through providing affordable housing to slum
dwellers the Chandigarh city would attain the distinction of being the first slum-free city
in the country. (Para 3.7.47)
The Committee came to know that some areas of the city experience floods during
heavy rains due to improper and inadequate drainage system. The UT Administration and
Municipal Corporation of Chandigarh should ensure checking of dumping of debris and
garbage into the open drainage, illegal encroachment of natural water courses etc. so that
the problem of flood could be solved. The proposed draft Master Plan 2031 should also
address this issue.
(Para 3.7.50)
The Committee understands that Chandigarh is known for its famous Sukhna Lake
which is the most-visited tourist place in the area. With the lake not getting enough water
due to poor monsoon, it turns into a dried bed. As it is completely a rainfed lake
occasionally drying up due to periodic occurrence of deficit rainfall. The Committee
recommends that a think tank should be involved in this matter. Besides, There should be
a permanent body for its conservation and monitoring and its members should be drawn
from experts from the field of hydrology, soil, ecology, wildlife etc. A long term plan may
be prepared for conserving the lake. (Para 3.7.53)
The Committee is of the view that while implementing the provisions of Electricity
Act, 2003 efforts should be made to protect the interests of the public and employees.
(Para 3.8.4)
The Committee desires that the issue of inadequacy of staff and equipments in the

63
Electricity Department may be resolved at the earliest. (Para 3.8.7)
The Committee recommends that UT Administration should conduct examination for
the recruitment of Conductors at the earliest. Besides, recruitment notification for vacant
posts of workshop staff, management staff, and Class-IV staff should also be advertised
soon and filled up at the earliest. (Para 3.9.3)
The Committee is of the view that the UT Administration should complete the
process for procuring new buses without any procedural delay. The Committee believes that
non-availability of buses against sanctioned fleet will add woes to commuters. (Para 3.9.6)
The Committee recommends that the UT Administration should resolve the issue of
pay fixation of the employees as per rules at the earliest. The Committee would like to be
apprised of action taken in this regard. (Para 3.9.9)

Health Insurance Scheme for health cover of

6.0 The Administrator, Lakshadweep Islands thereafter made a presentation on the UT of
Lakshadweep. The Main features of the presentation are as below:
● The islands with an area of 32 sq. km. have a total coastline of 132 km. in the Arabian
Sea. It has a group of 11 islands, Kalpeni and Bitra being the nearest and the farthest
islands at distances of 287 and 483 kms. respectively. 10 islands are inhabitated with
a population of 0.64 lakh. Majority population is Muslim and only one per cent belong
to other community. The population density as per 2011 Census is 2013 per sq. km.
against national average of 382 with sex ratio at 946 and zero maternal mortality rate,
100% immunisation and 6.51 infant mortality rate against 3.01 and 47.57 national rates
respectively. The birth rate and death rate also stand at 11.81 and 3.61 against national
average of 20.97 and 7.48 respectively. There are 10 village panchayats and one
district panchayat.

84
● The total literacy rate is 92.28% with male and female literacy rates standing at
96.55% and 88.25% respectively. The gross enrolment ratio of children aged 6-12
years is 99.01% with zero dropouts and the pupil-teacher ratio at 18.
● For ferrying passengers and goods, 25 vessels are operated by Lakshadweep Development
Corporation Limited, which include 7 Passenger Ships, 10 High Speed Vessels, 6 Cargo
Barges (including LPG carrier) and 2 Bollard Pull Tugs. 6 Monthly schedule for ships and
weekly schedule finalized by the Transport Committee with public representatives is
published. 2 x 400 Pax ships, One 2000 LPG carrier, 150T oil barge, 2 Nos. 800 MT
Multipurpose Cargo V essels, 1000T oil barge are also planned to be acquired.
● The work of dedicated Berth at Kochi has already been completed by the Cochin Port
Trust and is ready for operation. The construction of dedicated berth at Beypore will
be done by CPWD and MOU has been entered with Kerala Government for waterfront
area lease. DPR and EIA studies are being done and proposal will be submitted to the
Ministry for SFC approval. In principal approval of Karnataka Government has been
obtained for dedicated berth at Mangalore and MOU will be signed shortly.
● In order to embark the passengers directly to the islands, it was planned to construct
eastern side jetties in 4 islands viz. Kavaratti, Minicoy, Agatti and Amini. The Jetties
at Minicoy and Agatti has been made operational and the other 2 will be completed by
May 2013.
● There are 69 educational institutions, consisting 19 Pre-Primary Schools, 23 Primary
Schools, 10 Upper Primary Schools, 11 Senior Secondary Schools, 1 Kendriya
Vidyalaya, 1 Navodaya Vidyalaya, 3 University Centers and 1 DIET. A total of 14560
students were enrolled for 2013-14 academic session. Different Programmes viz.
strengthening of ICT education, Mid-Day Meal, allotment of seats for higher education,
scholarship to students, creation of infrastructure in schools, etc. are being undertaken
by the UT Administration. School students studying in Lakshadweep are provided free
text book, writing materials and uniform besides retention scholarship of R150/- and
R375/- per month for class VIII to X standard and XI to XII standard respectively.
Meritorious ST students are given scholarships ranging between R 400 to 
R1000
depending on the class and percentage of marks obtained in the Examinations.
● A total number of 134 seat are received from Central pool which include 12 seats for
MBBS, 2 seats for BDS, 3 for BAMS, 2 for BHMS, 3 BSc. Agriculture, 2 BVSc, 60
Engineering Degree, 50 Diploma Engineering. Besides, 2485 seats are received from
State Government of Kerala and other universities. However about one third of the
allotment of seats is being availed of during the last few years.
● Students of UT of Lakshadweep staying in college hostel whether in the mainland or
islands are paid full reimbursement of hostel expenses on the basis of the bills
presented by the hostel authorities. Students perusing study staying outside the hostel
in mainland/island their own arrangement are paid reimbursement at the prescribed
applicable rates of the UT Administration. Proposal for enhancement of scholarship for
students who are staying outside hostel at their own arrangements has been submitted
to the Ministry of HRD.
● Regarding health facilities, there are 2 hospitals, 3 CHCs, 4 PHCs, 2 F ACs and 14
sub centres, Ayush care is provided in all Islands and to provide specialty care, Rajiv
Gandhi Specialty Hospital has been set up in Agatti under PPP mode.
● R1000 per month is being given to 2155 old aged, destitute, widow, abandoned ladies,
invalid and disabled persons. 313 persons were given assistance for Haj pilgrimage.

85
● 100% population is dependent on PDS, which is functioning fairly well with the help
of 38 Fair Price Shops with adequate supplies of rice, sugar, kerosene. Regular LPG
supply has been ensured due to procurement of new vessel and FCI godown in
Andrott has stated recently to maintain stock during monsoon.
● Apart from the normal functions given to PRIs, 5 departments namely, health,
education, agriculture, animal husbandry, fisheries have been completely devolved to
them from April 2012 onwards. Island level 5 year plan and annual plan done through
gram sabha for the first time and total funds of Rs.196.304 (
R82.64 crores under Plan
and R113.670 crores under Non Plan) spent through PRIs.
● The project of extension of runway at Agatti has been approved by the MoEF and
environmental clearance has been obtained. AAI has prepared the DPR. UT
administration will complete the land acquisition at the earliest. The project is
specialized one, first-of-its-kind in India, because it will take the runway into the
lagoon through a specialized method.
● Bandwidth required for strategic as well as for disaster management communication.
BSNL is ready to provide now but with very high cost. BSNL has asked for 40 crore
Capex and 30 crore recurring for providing 100 Mbps additional bandwidth. Increasing
the Bandwidth in the islands still remains unresolved. UTL has requested Ministry of
Information Technology to provide it in their budget. Increasing the Bandwidth in the
islands still remains unresolved.
● Though there is no open defecation in the islands, contamination of groundwater is very
high due to intrusion of human excreta. Piped sewerage system is not possible as there
is no slope. To tackle this, the administration has tendered and approved the DRE
technology bio-toilets, 12000 numbers to be placed in all the islands. On completion,
UTL will be the first territory to have complete sewage management system.
● Groundwater (sub soil water) is the only natural resource of drinking water in the
Island of Lakshadweep. Providing quality drinking water is a major challenge. To
overcome the issue, the UT Administration proposed to install Low Temperature
Thermal Desalination (LTTD) Plants of 1 Lakh litre capacity in all the Islands. With
the help of NIOT, LTTD plants have been completed in three islands namely Kavaratti,
Agatti and Minicoy. Approval of Central Government to set up 6 more LTTD Plants
in other islands of Lakshadweep is expected shortly.
● There is a Water sports Club and a Diving Academy in Lakshadweep and facilities are
available for Snorkeling, Scuba diving, Jet-Skiing, Glass-bottom boats etc. Creation of
more infrastructures for tourism like Government Guest Houses, Eco-friendly Resorts
and Island resorts are required. Opening of un-inhabitated Islands for Toilrist purpose,
Promotion of Cruise Tourism, foreign yachts is being considered. Notifying additional
custom ports for foreign tourists is required. Upgradation of Water sport Institute into
a national level institute is also required.

INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home
Affairs, having been authorized by the Committee to submit the Report on its behalf, do hereby
present this One Hundred Eighty First Report on Action Taken by Government on the
recommendations/observations contained in the 180 th Report on Administration of Union
Territories (Daman & Diu, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Chandigarh).
2. The One Hundred and Eightieth Report of the Department-related Parliamentary
Standing Committee on Home Affairs was presented to Rajya Sabha and laid on the Table of
Lok Sabha on 19 th February, 2014. After presentation of the Report, the copies thereof were
sent to the Ministry of Home Affairs requesting them to furnish Action Taken Notes on the
recommendations of the Committee contained in the Report. The Ministry furnished the Action
Taken Notes on the said report to the Committee on 22 nd October, 2014.
3. The Committee first considered the draft Statement on Action Taken Notes furnished
by the Ministry of Home Affairs on the recommendations of the Committee contained in its
180th report in its sitting held on 20th November, 2014. The Committee, thereafter, considered
Action Taken Notes and the draft 181 st Acticon Taken Report on the recommendations/
observations contained in the 180 th Report on Administration of Union Territories (Daman &
Diu, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Chandigarh) and adopted the same in its meeting held on 4 th
December, 2014.

CHAPTER I
RECOMMENDATIONS/OBSERV ATIONS WHICH HA VE BEEN
ACCEPTED BY THE GOVERNMENT
DADRA AND NAGAR HA VELI
Recommendation
1.1 The construction of ring road in Silvassa Town area is necessary as there has been fast
increase in population growth in recent period. The Ministry of Road Transport and Highways
should accord early clearance for proposed construction of Ring Road. Besides, the UT
Administration should also make endeavour to improve existing road network as well as
construction of new roads for improving connectivity which will help fast flow of goods and
services. (Para 1.2.4  of 180 th Report )
Action Taken
1.1.1 The SFC proposal for construction of 4.3 Km. Ring Road (Phase-I) in Silvassa
amounting to `47.99 crore was submitted to the Ministry of Road Transport & Highway vide
letter dated 26.8.2013 and regularly followed up vide reminders dated 4.9.2013, 13.1.2014.
1.1.2 The UT Administration had then forwarded the proposal for construction of Ring Road
for Silvassa town amounting to Rs.48.58 Crore to MHA on 7.5.2014 in pursuance to its O.M.
No. 19011/08/2014-Fin.I dated 25.3.2014.
1.1.3 The Financial powers of Administrator DD & DNH have been increased up to Rs.50
Crore and accordingly the relevant papers/files have been sent to the UT Administration for
their consideration and approval.

1.10 The Committee is aware of the fact that despite India being an attractive investment
destination, entire exercise of the procedure and legal formalities make it tedious and
confusing. The Committee is of the view that long legal formalities and procedural delays make
frustrating impact on the investors. The Committee recommends that UT Administration should
introduce single window composite application form for all the procedural clearances such as
acquiring land, granting of construction permission, pollution control procedures, issuing
occupancy certificates, power allocation, environment and forest clearances and other licences/
registration which would make this region investment friendly and boost industrial growth in
the UT. The Committee also recommends that suggestions/views of representatives of Industry
and trade associations should also be taken into account while framing policies and laws
pertaining to industries as they are the people who know what are the bottlenecks coming in
their way. The Committee also recommends that the Ministry of Home Affairs should positively
consider the demands of representatives of trade and industry as subsidies given would provide
stimuli for further industrialization. (Para 1.4.9 ibid )

Recommendation
Project e-Sampark
1.24 The Committee understands that E-governance is two-way communication process
where benefits/services are delivered to people without procedural delays. In any citizen-centric
democratic system, cutting down on unwanted processes of too many layers while delivering
governmental services helps fast and targeted delivery while checking leakage. The Committee
recommends that the UT Administration should open more e-sampark centres in the city and
bring more Departments and services under its ambit. (Para 3.2.10 ibid )
Action Taken
1.24.1 Chandigarh Administration has strengthened its network of e-Sampark centres by
opening 10 new e-Sampark kiosks during the year 2013-14. e-Sampark kiosks are unique
public services delivery outlets. The uniqueness in the kiosk based public services delivery
concept is that the infrastructural as well as operations costs are significantly low and
these kiosks can be set up in areas quickly where space is a constraint. A new fully
fledged Sampark Centre was also opened in Sector 7 during the year 2013-14. As a new
initiative, Chandigarh Administration has introduced Railway Booking services through
e-Sampark Centres. Other newly introduced services include Aadhaar Enrollment and
payment of Property Tax. e-District Mission Mode Project (MMP) of the Government of
India which aims at electronic delivery of services is being implemented in Chandigarh.
Chandigarh Administration has identified 64 services which will be delivered through its
network of e-Sampark Centres, thus adding to existing bouquet of services offered by the
Sampark Centres. Once fully operational, residents of Chandigarh would be able to avail
certain key services in a time bound manner. Under e-District, services of the various
Departments of Chandigarh Administration would come under the ambit of e-Sampark
Centres. These include services of departments like Deputy Commissioner (DC) Office,
Registration and Licensing Authority (RLA), Education, Election, Food and Civil Supplies
etc. Chandigarh Administration is at an advanced stage of introducing RLA services through
Sampark Centres. A proposal to facilitate BSNL mobile to-ups service through e-Sampark
Centres is also being considered.

Recommendation
Misuse charges at R500/- per sq.ft. per month
2.4 The revised rates carry the sanctity of law as on date to serve as a deterrent to
unauthorized conversion of activities. The UT Administration should undertake downward
revision of the charges on priority basis and notify the same at the earliest.
(Para 3.5.12 ibid )

32
Action Taken
2.4.1 The levy to misuse charges is as per the provisions contained in section 15 of the
Capital of Punjab (Development and Regulation) Act 1952, which reads as under :-
(i) Penalty for breach of rules:  Except as otherwise provided for in this Act, any
contravention of any of the rules framed there under shall be punishable with
fine which may extend to five hundred rupees, in case of a continuing
contravention, with an additional fine, which may extend to twenty rupees, for
each day during which such contravention continues after the first conviction;
and the Court while passing any sentence on conviction of any person for the
contravention of any rule, may direct that any property or part thereof in
respect of which the rule has been contravened, shall be forfeited to the
(Central Government).
(ii) The misuse charges fixed way back in 1952 had lost their deterrent effect and
accordingly the rates were revised in the year 2007 to R500/- square feet per
month as under :-
(iii)  Procedure in case of building violations and/or misuse of site/building
(a) When a building violation(s) and/or misuse of a site or building under
rule 9, is reported or comes to the notice of the Estate Officer then,
without prejudice to any action taken under Section 8-A of the Act, a
notice of period not less than 15 days shall be served on the allottee/
lessee(s) and on the occupier(s) of the site or building requiring that the
allottee/lessee(s) and the occupier(s) shall within a period of two
months, remove the said building violation(s) and/or misuse and pay
monthly charges @ R500/- per sq. ft. of area under building violation(s)
and/or misuse, which shall be paid jointly and severally by the transferee
and the occupier of the site or building for every month or part thereof
the building violation(s) and/or misuse occurs.
(b) The decision of the UT Administration to revise the misuse charges to
R500/- by making an amendment in the Rules had come up before the
Hon’ble High Court of Punjab and Haryana at Chandigarh. Even though
the main Act viz.  Capital of Punjab (Development & Regulation) Act
1952 fixed the misuse charges way back at R20/- only, the Hon’ble
High Court has not set aside the amendments in the Rules made by the
UT Administration fixing the misuse charges at R500/-per sq. ft. per
month on the area under building violation.
(c) The High Court had also directed that necessary action should be taken
to amend the Act. The UT Administration is examining the matter to
make a proposal to the MHA for undertaking the requisite amendment in
the main Act of 1952. As the Capital of Punjab (Development &
Regulation) Act 1952 was enacted long back, it was also intended to

33
consider making comprehensive changes in the Act in some of the areas
in view of the changed scenario and to suit the current requirement of
the Administration.
(d) In fact the Second Administrative Reforms Commission has also
recommended in its 15 th Report that the UT Administration should revisit
the Capital of Punjab (Development & Regulation) Act and the Punjab
New Capital (Periphery control) Act, 1952 to align them with the
changed circumstances. As the matter is complex, it is taking some time
to make the required reference to the Ministry of Home Affairs.
(e) The UT is constituting a committee to draft the changes required to be
made in the law in regard to the above and a proposal shall be submitted
to MHA, GOI in the near future.

small facility will not do. The Committee desires that the MHA should pursue with

62
Ministry of External Affairs for opening a Passport Seva Kendra either in Daman or
Silvasa at the earliest as it would cater to the needs of both the UTs within a time
frame of three months. (3.8.3)
Regularization of Daily Wage Employees
The Committee is displeased to note that the Ministry is not sympathetically
considering the plight of those working on daily wages/adhoc/contract basis. The
Committee is unable to understand why a condition has been put in place for these
workers that they should not have been overage when they were engaged for the post
they are working on. After all, they were engaged by the government agencies. The
Committee recommends that these daily wages/adhoc/contract workers should be
regularised at the earliest. (3.9.3)
CHANDIGARH
Smart School
The Committee is not happy to note that only two smart schools have been setup.
The Committee recommends that the UT Administration should take up this issue of
upgradation of existing schools into smart schools on priority. The Committee would also
like to be apprised of status of five schools which were to be upgraded as smart schools
in 2014-15. (3.10.2)
Conversion of Industrial Plots From Lease Holds Tenure to Free Hold Tenure
The Committee is not satisfied with the plain reply of the Ministry and would
like to reiterate its recommendation for conversion of industrial plots from lease hold
tenure to free hold tenure. (3.11.2)
Single Window System
The reply does not address the issue of Single Window Committee. The
Committee again recommends that the Single Window Committee should be made
functional and it should be ensured that the common citizens should get their services
delivers hassle free. (3.12.2)
Allowing Need Bases Changes in The Industrial Plot
The Committee is not satisfied with the reply of the Ministry. The Committee
reiterates its recommendation that the Master Plan should address the issue and
grievance of the industries appropriately. The Committee understands that a need to
cover the open spaces with corrugated sheets to prevent the raw material from bad
weather, theft and rains is sometimes required and need based internal changes in the
buildings and temporary coverage in the court-yard to protect material from being
damaged by weather should be permitted. (3.13.2)

63
Automobile Service Stations
The Committee is not convinced with the response given by the Ministry.
Violators can be punished but on this pretext service stations cannot be prevented from
carrying out their activities. The Committee reiterates that the UT administration
should reconsider its decision for allowing the automobile service stations in the
industrial area. (3.14.2)
Inadequate Health Care Facilities
The Committee is not happy to note that the proposal is still at consideration.
There should be a time-frame fixed and decision should be taken within the time
frame. (3.15.2)
Lack of Civic Amenities in Southern Sectors
The Committee earlier recommended for improvement of amenities as they
cannot wait for finalization of Master Plan. The Committee, therefore, again
recommends that problems of basic civic amenities like roads, drainage systems; street
lights, parks, markets, bus shelters, primary health centers, post office, community
centers, etc. in southern sectors of the city should be taken up as day to day municipal
and administrative work and all above said amenities should be improved. (3.16.5)
DADRA AND NAGAR HA VELI
Municipal Drinking Water Supply Project, Silvassa
The Committee recommends that the Ministry should impress upon the Ministry
of Drinking Water and Sanitation and Ministry of Finance for early administrative
approval of Integrated Water Management Plan and expenditure sanction respectively
and seek their comments/views/decisions with six months. The Committee would like to
be informed of the projected time-frame for completion of Water Supply Scheme for the
Silvassa and Amli Township and the project for Piped Water Supply in interior area of
Mandoni and Dudhani. (4.1.7)
New Hospital Building, Khanvel
The Committee would like to be apprised of the progress regarding
construction of 100 bedded Sub-District Hospital at Khanvel, in the UT of Dadra &
Nagar Haveli. (4.2.2)
Issue Pertaining to Industries (Tax Exemption)
The Committee recommends that the Ministry of Home Affairs should take up
this matter with Ministry of Finance on priority basis as not extending exemption of tax
benefits to the UT of Dadra & Nagar Haveli may lead to exodus of industries from there
and hence could lead to low industrial output, unemployment and labour unrest. The
Committee also recommends that the comments/views/decisions of the Ministry of
Finance should be sought with six months. (4.3.2)

64
The Committee feels that the matter should be pursued vigorously with Ministry
of Power for restoring 25MW power back to the UT of Dadra & Nagar Haveli and the
matter should be clinched within six months. (4.4.2)
Eco-Sensitive Zones
The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry and recommends that the
Committee should be informed of the status of approval by the Ministry of Environment
& Forest for sparing 100 mtrs. as eco-sensitive zone. The Committee also recommends
that the Ministry of Environment and Forest should be requested to give their
comments/views/decisions within six months. (4.5.3)
DAMAN & DIU
Assembly For The U.T. of Daman & Diu And Dadra & Nagar Haveli
The Committee reiterates its recommendation and feels that the Ministry of
Home Affairs should consider the proposal in view of popular demand. The Committee
desires to be informed of the status of progress in the matter. (4.6.3)
Setting UP Of High Court, Mumbai Bench
The Ministry should pursue the matter vigorously with the Ministry of law and
their views on the matter should be sought at the earliest. (4.7.2)
National Stadium For The U.T. Of Daman & Diu
The Committee recommends that the identification of land should be expedited
and other procedural delays should be minimized so that the proposed stadium comes up
soon. The Committee would also like to be apprised of the time-frame as to by when
the establishment of national stadium will be completed. (4.8.2)
Ferry Boat Servives From Mumbai To Diu Via Daman
The Committee would like to be informed of the progress regarding feasibility
study. The Committee recommends that feasibility assessment should be done at the
earliest. (4.9.2)
CHANDIGARH
Chandigarh Small Flat Scheme 2006
The Committee recommends that the construction of 4960 flats at Maloya-I should be
completed at the earliest and decision regarding remaining flats at Maloya-I, Maloya-II
and Mauli Jagran-I, should be taken without waiting for allotment & utilization of the
flats at Maloya-I. The Committee desires that completion of these projects should be
done within projected time-frame. (4.10.3)

65
Rajiv Gandhi Chandigarh Technology Park (RGCTP)
The Committee desires that early decision may be taken for allotting 39 acres of
land. The other infrastructure should also be created in a time bound manner. (4.11.3)
Railway
The Committee while noting the reply recommends that MHA should impress
upon Ministry of Railways for running new trains or extending more running trains to-
and-fro via  Chandigarh. The Committee also recommends that the comments/views/
decisions of the Ministry of Railways should be asked for within six months and the
Committee should be apprised of it. (4.12.2)
Ownership Rights To The Residents Of The Tenement Colonies
The Committee in view of the reply of the Ministry recommends that the
Ministry should impress upon UT Administration to positively consider the issue of
transfer of ownership rights on lease-hold basis to those having documents like GPA and
other evidence of transaction and transfer of possession. The Committee recommends
that the decision may be taken within three months and Committee may be informed
of the decision. (4.13.2)
Allowing Transfer On GPA Basis
The Committee notes the reply of the Ministry and would like to be apprised
of the consideration status by Chandigarh Housing Board (CHB) for granting of one
time relaxation for transfer of dwelling units sold by the allottee within the lock-
in-period of 5 years on GPA executed on or before 11.10.2011 in favour of GPA
Holder. The Committee desires that the decision may be taken within a specified
time-frame. (4.14.2)
SHORTAGE OF POWER
The Committee desires that the matter may be taken up with Ministry of Power
and CEA for early finalization of the proposal and approval. There should be a time
frame for this. (4.15.2)
Shortage Of Drinking Water
The Committee desires that laying of additional diameter pipeline should be
completed as per the schedule fixed. There should be no delay. (4.17.6)
Drying Up Of Sukhna Lake
The Committee desires that the matter may be pursued with National Institute
of Hydrology (NIH) for completing the study as per the time schedule fixed so the work
may start soon. (4.18.2)

66
Inadequacy Of Staff
The Committee would like to be apprised about the progress and time-frame
decided regarding filling up of 42 posts of LDC in Electricity Department in UT of
Chandigarh. (4.19.2)
Vacant Posts
The Committee desires that the recruitment for management staff should be
completed as per the time-frame fixed and there should be no delay in this regard.
(4.20.3)

2.0 At the outset, the Chairman welcomed the Members to the meeting and informed them
of the agenda of the meeting i.e.  to consider the Action Taken by the Government on the
recommendations contained in 180 th  Report of the Committee on Home Affairs on the
Administration of Union Territories (Daman & Diu, Dadra & Nagar Haveli and Chandigarh). He
also briefed them about the work done by the previous Committee. He further informed that
the Action taken by the Government on the recommendations contained the Report had been
received, which had been analyzed and categorized and the statement thereon with further
recommendations of this Committee had been circulated to the Members. He asked Members
to give their suggestions so that the Secretariat could incorporate the same appropriately while
preparing Action Taken Report.
3.0 With regard to recommendations concerning UT of Chandigarh, one Member was of
the view that implementation on recommendations concerning some issues like e-Sampark
centres, MSMED Act, conversion of industrial plots, allowing transfer on General Power of
Attorney basis, Single Window System was poor and on the ground the reality was quite
different. She also mentioned about skewed teacher pupil ratio in schools. The Member also
mentioned that the colonies of the slum dwellers were being demolished, but new flats were
not being allotted. It is proposed that it would be done through a one-time biometric survey,
but only thumb impressions were being taken. She also mentioned that street vendors, who
had been working there for the last thirty years, were being removed even after enactment
of the Street V endors Act.
4.0 One Member raised the issue of parking problems in Chandigarh and suggested to
tackle the problem in the Master Plan. He also mentioned that ratio of employees in
Chandigarh should be maintained as 60:40 as was decided at the time of partition of Punjab
and Haryana; however these employees are being sent from Centre (DANICS). However one
Member intervened and suggested for reservation to local people of Chandigarh in
employment. She also suggested that pay scales should be at par with pay scales in Punjab
and Haryana.
5.0 One Member drew attention to the Action Taken on the Recommendation concerning
Passport Seva Kendra either in Daman or Silvassa may not be treated as accepted and instead
be treated as pending. Another Member suggested that the Committee should recommend for
some time limit in respect of the projects or works which were to be taken up or were
continuing. One Member suggested that Anti-defection Act should be made applicable in Daman
and Diu municipality before next elections are held. He was of the view that Daman and Diu
being a small territory should be covered under CRZ-2 Area.
6.0 One Members was of the view that some UTs such as Puducherry has many outlying
areas as part of that Union Territory like Mahe in Kerala; Yanam in Andhra Pradesh and there
are no clear demarcated borders. The adjoining States have a different excise policy resulting
various implications especially during enforcement of code of conduct during elections. He
suggested that Committee should examine this issue. Intervening in the discussion, one Member
suggested that these small pockets should be amalgamated with the provinces in which they
exist. The Chairman assured that this issue will be looked into during the examination of the
functioning of those UTs.

71

by cyclone in Andhra Pradesh. Several Members felt that the Committee should visit the
cyclone (Hudhud) affected areas.

INTRODUCTION
I, the Chairman of the Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home
Affairs having been authorised by the Committee to submit the report on its behalf, do hereby
present this One Hundred Eighty Second Report on the Rescue, Rehabilitation and
Reconstruction plan in the aftermath of the floods and landslides in Jammu and Kashmir.
2. The Department-related Parliamentary Standing Committee on Home Affairs, in its
meeting held on 10th October, 2014, taking note of the unprecedented devastation caused by
rains and floods in Jammu and Kashmir, heard the presentation of the Home Secretary and
representatives of the Government of Jammu and Kashmir on the subject.
3. The Committee while finalizing its report, relied on the following papers/documents:-
(i) Background note furnished by the Ministry of Home Affairs; and
(ii) Replies to the queries of Members raised during its sittings.
4. The Committee in its sitting held on 4 th December, 2014 considered and adopted the
present report.
5. For facility of reference and convenience, Observations and Recommendations of the
Committee have been printed in bold letters in the body of the Report.
P. BHATTACHARYA
Chairman,
